areas.area: Chase camera behaviour and camera collision
areas.summary:
I compared holtburger-web's follow camera with OpenAC's RetailChaseCamera, PhysicsCameraCollisionProbe and their tests, using the retail decomp as the authority. Holtburger files: scene3d/camera.js, camera_math.js, viewer_cell.js, ui/camera_settings.js, and the spatial/transition crates behind the wasm sweeps. Decomp functions: CameraManager::UpdateCamera, CameraSet::*, SmartBox::update_viewer/set_viewer and CPhysicsObj::FindObjCollisions.

These pieces are already ported correctly: the zoom continuum constants, the near-fade curve, the stiffness fraction, FilterMouseInput, the 0.18 m in-head offset and the +/-0.8 mouselook limit.

The divergences are in how the parts fit together:
1. First person is not tied to the character: the view ignores the character's heading, and mouse drag does not turn the character.
2. Collision and smoothing run in the wrong order, and the view direction is taken from the collided eye. This tilts the view when the camera is pulled in, pops it back out in one frame, and lets the camera lag behind walls when stiffness is on.
3. There is no single retail viewer transit. Terrain is a vertical clamp at the eye instead of a sweep, scenery (trees, rocks) is never tested, and the viewer cell is computed in a second walk.
4. The collision standoff is 0.7 m instead of retail's 0.3 m, and the pivot is 1.6 m instead of 1.5 m.
5. Auto-follow ignores turns in place.
6. Slope alignment is missing.

Not reported as findings, because ui/camera_settings.js keeps them on purpose and they are the owner's decision: the default 6 m boom that looks down at the player (retail is 2.61 m on (0,-2.5,0.75), looking level along the heading), the hard-locked default stiffness (retail 0.45), and the 15 m distance slider (retail Farther refuses |x| or |y| > 10). No camera items are open in PARITY-STATUS.json or in the 2026-10-04 comparison docs.

findings.title: First-person (in-head) view is decoupled from the character: Q/E turns do not rotate the view and mouse-X does not turn the character
findings.decomp_evidence: CameraSet::SetInHead acclient.c:149230: SetTranslationalStiffness(1.0), SetTargetDirection((0,1,0)) and viewer_offset (0,0.18,0) in the pivot frame. CameraManager::UpdateCamera builds pivot_frame from the player's frame or plane direction (`Position::localtoglobalvec((Position*)&v8[6], ..., &v3->direction)`). So the in-head eye and look direction follow the player heading, damped only by r_stiffness. CameraSet::Rotate acclient.c:148788, in-head branch (offset == (0,0.18,0)): `headinga = CPhysicsObj::get_heading(v18); v19 = headinga + 8.0;` (:148903), then cmdinterp TurnToHeading, i.e. the CHARACTER turns 8 degrees per step. With m_UseMouseTurning it issues TurnRight/TurnLeft 0x6500000D/0x6500000E (:148942). CameraSet::MouseLookHandler :149300-149340 sends mouse X into Rotate(..., camera_keys=0).
findings.openac_evidence: RetailChaseCamera.cs:134 ComputeInHeadPose(pivotWorld, heading, ...) uses the player-yaw heading, and :525 places the eye at `pivotWorld + headingForward * RetailFirstPersonForward`. RetailChaseCamera.cs:258-260: AdjustYaw in head does `_pendingFirstPersonRotate += adjustment`. CameraFrameController.cs:113 and :146-153 pass this to TryTakeFirstPersonTurn, then RequestTurnToHeading(heading +/- 8 degrees). Tests: RetailChaseCameraTests.cs:1000 AdjustYawInFirstPerson_StaysInTheHeadAndAsksTheCharacterToTurn and :778 SecondUpdate_FirstPerson_SnapsTranslationAndOnlyDampsRotation.
findings.holt_evidence: camera.js:1707-1708 `_positionInHead(p) { const fx = Math.sin(this.followYaw);` builds both the eye offset and the look direction from followYaw. camera.js:1084 `if (this._retailZoomOn && this._inHead) return; // first-person: yaw = look dir` turns off auto-follow in head. camera.js:887 right-drag only does `this.followYaw += mx * POINTER_YAW_SENS * ...`. Movement is player-local (camera.js computeMovementFromKeys, 'WASD now drives in the player's local body frame').
findings.discrepancy: In holtburger first person, turning with Q/E rotates the body but leaves the view fixed. Mouse-X drag swings the view but not the body, so after looking around, W walks in a different direction from where you are looking. The 0.18 m eye offset also follows the free yaw, not the head. In retail the in-head view is rigidly tied to the player heading (rotation damped by stiffness), and mouse or rotate input turns the character in 8 degree TurnToHeading steps.
findings.proposed_change: In _positionInHead, take the yaw from the character: `const yaw = this._playerHeadingForFollow() ?? this.followYaw;`. Write it back to this.followYaw so that leaving the head keeps continuity. Use it for both the eye offset (IN_HEAD_FORWARD_M) and the look vector. Keep followPitch and clampInHeadDirZ for vertical look. In onMouseMove (camera.js:~887), when `this._retailZoomOn && this._inHead`, do not add to followYaw. Instead accumulate `mx * POINTER_YAW_SENS * this._mouseSensMult`. Each time the accumulator passes 8 degrees (0.13963 rad), call `sessionHandle.turnToHeading(pose.heading -/+ 0.13963)` and subtract the step. The sign follows followYaw = -pose.heading: dragging right lowers pose.heading. turnToHeading uses the CCW pose.heading convention, the same as headingFromTurnQuat in scene3d/server_turn.js. Optional: when camStiffness is set, slerp only the in-head ROTATION, as retail keeps r_stiffness while t_stiffness = 1. Put the pure step logic in camera_math.js (`inHeadTurnSteps(accum) -> {steps, rest}`).
findings.test_plan: node apps/holtburger-web/tests/camera_retail_math.test.cjs. (1) Pure tests for inHeadTurnSteps: an accumulator of 0.2 rad gives 1 step and a remainder of 0.0604; a negative accumulator gives negative steps; the step equals 8 degrees. (2) Static source assertions: _positionInHead calls _playerHeadingForFollow, and the onMouseMove in-head branch calls turnToHeading and does not add to followYaw. The existing assertion `_positionInHead\(p\);\s*\n\s*return;` still holds.

findings.title: Collision runs before smoothing and the view is aimed from the collided eye; retail smooths toward the uncollided pose, then sweeps, and keeps the sought orientation
findings.decomp_evidence: SmartBox::PlayerPhysicsUpdatedCallback acclient.c:144049 calls `CameraManager::UpdateCamera(cm, &result, &this->viewer)`: it interpolates FROM the collided viewer (`Frame::interpolate_origin(&actual_pos.frame, &v9->frame, &camera_frame, t_frac)` :147841, `interpolate_rotation(... r_frac)` :147842; frac = stiffness*quantum*10). The target is the UNCLIPPED camera_frame (:147763 pivot_frame.localtoglobal(viewer_offset); orientation set at :147799 from target_direction, which is the heading, or pivot minus the unclipped origin under LOOK_AT_PIVOT :147767). The result becomes viewer_sought_position. SmartBox::update_viewer :144991 then sweeps pivot to sought with init_object(player, 92 = IS_VIEWER|PATH_CLIPPED|FREE_ROTATE|PERFECT_CLIP) (:145086) and publishes `set_viewer(&sphere_path.curr_pos)` (:145091). FREE_ROTATE snaps curr_pos orientation to end_pos up front (ported in holtburger-dat driver_validate.rs:378-384). Net effect: collision only moves the eye position, pull-in is immediate, re-extension is damped, and the view direction never depends on the collided eye. Default stiffness is 0.45 (CameraManager ctor :147898, 1055286886 = 0.45f).
findings.openac_evidence: RetailChaseCamera.cs:151-164: `candidateEye = Vector3.Lerp(_publishedEye, targetEye, tAlpha)` (from the published, i.e. swept, eye toward the unclipped target), then `CollisionProbe.SweepEye(pivotWorld, _soughtEye, ...)`. :176 uses the damped forward from the unclipped pose: `CreateLookAt(publishedEye, publishedEye + _dampedForward, Z)`. Tests: RetailChaseCameraTests.cs:1493 Update_AfterClampReleases_EyeReExtendsGradually, :1542 Update_SweepTargetConvergesOntoContact_NotTheFullBoom, :1646 Update_PressedAgainstWall_EyeGlidesStably. CameraDiagnostics.cs:18/20 default stiffness is 0.45.
findings.holt_evidence: camera.js:1313 `const camera = this._clipCameraAgainstWorld(p, finalX, finalY, finalZ);` runs first. With stiffness set, camera.js:1382 `_applyStiffness(dt, finalX, ...)` lerps persp.position toward the CLIPPED target (:1749-1766). The hard-lock default is camera.js:1385 `this.persp.lookAt(...acToThree(lookX, lookY, lookZ))` from the clipped eye, with lookZ = p.z + 1.6 + lookLift (:1335). The guardLookHorizontal LIVE-03 patch (:1369) exists because a clipped eye can land on the head and give a vertical look vector. The camera_settings.js DEFAULTS comment says stiffness 1.0 is kept on purpose.
findings.discrepancy: (a) Hard-lock default: when an occluder clears (a pillar, doorframe or tree passes), the eye jumps back out by up to 6 m in one frame. Retail re-extends at about 7.5% per frame at 60 Hz. (b) When the eye is pulled in, its look vector to the fixed lookAt point steepens. At the default pitch of 0.3, a 30% pull-in tilts the view from about 22 degrees to about 42 degrees down, and a full pull-in gives the degenerate vertical basis. Retail's view direction does not change under collision. (c) With ?camStiffness or a user-set stiffness, the camera lerps from its old position (now behind the wall) toward the clipped target, so it spends about 0.5 s on the far side of geometry. Retail's sweep runs after the lerp, so the published eye is always valid.
findings.proposed_change: Restructure the follow branch of positionCamera. (1) Compute the ideal eye and the look point, including cast-bias, as today. Set `fwd = normalize(look - ideal)`: this is the sought orientation, independent of collision. (2) Smooth the POSITION before the sweep: `tFrac = stiffnessFrac(this._camStiffness ?? 1, dt)`, `sought = seeded && |prev - ideal| < STIFFNESS_TELEPORT_SNAP_M ? lerp(this._prevEyeAc, ideal, tFrac) : ideal`. (3) `eye = this._clipCameraAgainstWorld(p, sought...)`, then `this._prevEyeAc = eye` (in AC coordinates). (4) Publish `persp.position = acToThree(eye)` with orientation from `Matrix4.lookAt(eye, eye + fwd, up)`, slerped by rFrac when stiffness is set. Remove `_applyStiffness`'s position lerp toward the clipped target. Keep guardLookHorizontal as a backstop; it becomes inert because fwd comes from the ideal eye. Put the pure step in camera_math.js as `retailViewerStep(prevEye, idealEye, frac, sweepFn)`. Follow-up for the owner to decide (feel default): set the Camera-tab stiffness default to retail 0.45 instead of 1.0 (camera_settings.js DEFAULTS).
findings.test_plan: node apps/holtburger-web/tests/camera_retail_math.test.cjs. Add pure cases for retailViewerStep that mirror the OpenAC tests, using a fake sweep that clamps at x = -1. (a) Frame 1 publishes on the wall plane, never beyond it. (b) After the wall is removed, the next eye moves only frac (4.5*dt) of the way out. (c) While pressed against the wall, the per-frame delta over 30 frames is under 1e-3. (d) With frac = 1 (hard-lock), sought equals ideal. (e) The forward vector is identical with and without the clamp. Update the static assertions at lines ~248-260 that pin `_applyStiffness(dt, finalX` so they pin the new ordering: the sweep call appears after the lerp.
findings.already_tracked: no (the LIVE-03 guardLookHorizontal patch treats one symptom; camera_settings.js documents the hard-lock default as deliberate)

findings.title: Camera collision is a chain of 8 separate JS-to-wasm sweeps, not one retail viewer transit: terrain is clamped instead of swept, and scenery trees and rocks are never tested
findings.decomp_evidence: SmartBox::update_viewer acclient.c:144991-145110 runs one CTransition. start_cell = player cell, or AdjustPosition(pivot) when indoor (:145054). init_object(player, 92) (:145086), init_sphere(1, &viewer_sphere, 1.0) (:145087), init_path(start_cell, pivot, sought), find_valid_position. On success, viewer = curr_pos and viewer_cell = curr_cell (:145091-145092). Otherwise AdjustPosition(sought). Otherwise viewer = player position with viewer_cell = 0. The transit collides with everything in the cells it crosses: landcell terrain polygons, building and EnvCell BSPs, and every shadow object. CPhysicsObj::FindObjCollisions :316159 exempts only creatures for a viewer (`if (transition->object_info.state & 4 && weenie->IsCreature()) return 1`). Scenery has no weenie, so it collides.
findings.openac_evidence: PhysicsCameraCollisionProbe.cs:28-50: ResolveWithTransition(pivot to eye, sphere 0.3, IsViewer|PathClipped|FreeRotate|PerfectClip, skipping the self entity), then AdjustPosition(desiredEye), then (playerPos, 0). One call returns both eye and viewer cell. Tests: CameraCollisionIndoorTests.cs:28 SweepEye_OutdoorCell_StoppedByBuildingChannelShell, CameraCollisionUpdateViewerTests.cs:19 SweepEye_IndoorPivotInCellAboveFeet_SeatsStartAtPivotCell.
findings.holt_evidence: camera.js:1509 `handle.terrainHeightAt(finalX, finalY)` raises finalZ at the end point only (:1511). Steps 2-6 (:1560-1690) each cross into wasm separately: cameraSweepCollision, sweepSphereAgainstBuildingMesh, sweepSphereAgainstStatics (:1581, LandblockInfo stab AABBs only), sweepSphereAgainstCellMesh, sweepSphereAgainstCellStatics, sweepSphereAgainstEntities (:1652), clipCameraToCellSpace (:1673). No camera step calls SpatialScene::sweep_sphere_against_scenery (scene.rs:4361); its only users are the player path and tests. cells.js:2170 then walks the same segment again with resolveViewerCell. scene.rs:5038 says: 'We have no camera transit'. The faithful driver already supports IS_VIEWER (holtburger-dat driver_validate.rs:415-417, objectinfo.rs:95-96) and is used for the player in faithful_bridge.rs:1738-1761.
findings.discrepancy: (a) Procedural scenery has cylsphere physics that retail's camera collides with, but holtburger's camera passes through tree trunks and rocks. (b) Against slopes and ridges, holtburger lifts the eye vertically, which changes the view pitch, instead of pulling it in along the boom. A ridge between the pivot and the eye is never tested. (c) Two separate walks (clip chain at radius 0.5, viewer-cell walk at 0.3) can disagree about which cell the eye is in. (d) Up to 8 wasm crossings per frame plus a getRenderSet call.
findings.proposed_change: Stage 1 (S): add a wasm export `sweepSphereAgainstScenery(from, to, radius, landblockId)` in lib.rs wrapping SpatialScene::sweep_sphere_against_scenery, and call it as step 4b in _clipCameraAgainstWorld. Stage 2 (L): add `SpatialScene::viewer_transit(player_cell, pivot, sought) -> (eye, cell)` in faithful_bridge.rs. Model it on the existing bridge: object_info.state = IS_VIEWER|PATH_CLIPPED|FREE_ROTATE|PERFECT_CLIP (0x5C); one sphere {center 0, r 0.3}; start cell by AdjustPosition(pivot) when indoor; init_path(start_cell, Some(pivot), sought); find_valid_position; then the two retail fallbacks; an object overlay that skips creatures and the player. Export it as `viewerTransit(...) -> Float32Array[x, y, z, cell]`. In camera.js, call it once in place of steps 1-6, keeping the old chain behind `?camTransit=off`. In cells.js updateViewerCell, take the transit's cell instead of calling resolveViewerCell.
findings.test_plan: Rust #[test]s in crates/holtburger-world/src/spatial/tests.rs (orchestrator runs cargo test -p holtburger-world, capped). Reuse the scenery fixture near tests.rs:6102: viewer_transit_stops_at_scenery_cylsphere. Also: viewer_transit_terrain_ridge_pulls_in_along_boom (the eye ends on the pivot side of a ridge at the same heading, not raised), viewer_transit_crosses_portal_returns_neighbour_cell, and viewer_transit_invalid_start_falls_back_to_player_cell_zero. JS: a static assertion in tests/camera_retail_math.test.cjs that _clipCameraAgainstWorld calls viewerTransit when the flag is on; run node apps/holtburger-web/tests/viewer_cell.test.mjs for the cells.js wiring.
findings.already_tracked: no (scene.rs:5038 notes 'We have no camera transit' as a known gap; no open item)

findings.title: Collision standoff is 0.5 m sphere plus 0.2 m backoff from a 1.6 m pivot; retail clips a 0.3 m viewer sphere at contact from the 1.5 m pivot
findings.decomp_evidence: The viewer_sphere global (CSphere at VA 0x83CC14, ?viewer_sphere@@3VCSphere@@A) gets its radius at acclient.c:145543 `dword_83CC20 = 1050253722`, which is 0x3E99999A = 0.3f; center (0,0,0) at :145537-145542. PATH_CLIPPED in the transit stops at the first contact, with no extra backoff. The pivot is player + pivot_offset (0,0,CAMERA_DEFAULT_PIVOT_Z = 1.5) (acclient.c:39550; set in SetDefaultOffsets :149374 and Farther :149097; applied in update_viewer through localtoglobalvec).
findings.openac_evidence: PhysicsCameraCollisionProbe.cs:8 `ViewerSphereRadius = 0.3f`; the eye is the transit's position with no backoff (:44). RetailChaseCamera.cs:54 `PivotHeight = 1.5f`.
findings.holt_evidence: camera.js:1477-1478 `const CAM_RADIUS = 0.5; const BACKOFF = 0.2;`, :1541 `t = Math.max(0.0, hit.t - backoffT)`, :1511 `minZ = terrainZ + CAM_RADIUS + BACKOFF`, :1525 `const startZ = playerPos.z + 1.6;`. viewer_cell.js:40 VIEWER_SPHERE_RADIUS_M = 0.3 and :43 VIEWER_PIVOT_Z_M = 1.6, while the near-fade and in-head paths use CAMERA_DEFAULT_PIVOT_Z = 1.5 (camera.js near-fade block, _positionInHead).
findings.discrepancy: Every contact stops the eye about 0.4 m (along the boom) further from the surface than retail. In a 3 m-high dungeon room the shallow default boom meets the ceiling about 1 m closer to the player than in retail, which also triggers the near-fade more often. The viewer-cell walk (0.3 m) and the clip chain (0.5 m plus backoff) use different spheres on the same segment. The pivot is 1.6 m for the sweep and 1.5 m for the fade and in-head.
findings.proposed_change: In _clipCameraAgainstWorld, import VIEWER_SPHERE_RADIUS_M and set CAM_RADIUS = VIEWER_SPHERE_RADIUS_M (0.3). Set BACKOFF = 0, or at most a 0.02 m numerical skin. The near plane is 0.1 at 60 degrees FOV, so the frustum corner sits about 0.155 m away, inside 0.3. Change the terrain clamp to `terrainZ + CAM_RADIUS` and the start to `playerPos.z + CAMERA_DEFAULT_PIVOT_Z`. Set viewer_cell.js VIEWER_PIVOT_Z_M = 1.5 so both passes share one pivot and one sphere. Leave lookZ framing alone (owner framing). This is a quick interim step; camera-3 subsumes it if that lands.
findings.test_plan: node apps/holtburger-web/tests/camera_retail_math.test.cjs: add static assertions that camera.js sets CAM_RADIUS from VIEWER_SPHERE_RADIUS_M, that BACKOFF <= 0.02, and that startZ uses CAMERA_DEFAULT_PIVOT_Z. node apps/holtburger-web/tests/viewer_cell.test.mjs: it already derives the expected pivot from vc.VIEWER_PIVOT_Z_M (line 112), so it should stay green after the constant change; add `assert.equal(vc.VIEWER_PIVOT_Z_M, 1.5)`.

findings.title: Auto-follow does not follow in-place turns (turn-to-face on attack or cast, server turns, wasm pursuit turns)
findings.decomp_evidence: CameraManager::UpdateCamera acclient.c:147425-147842 rebuilds pivot_frame from the player's frame every update (localtoglobalvec(player m_position, direction); viewer_offset is pivot-local, :147763), with no 'is moving' gate. Any heading change, including the server-driven TurnToHeading/TurnToObject, swings the camera at r_stiffness*dt*10 (0.45 means a rate of 4.5/s).
findings.openac_evidence: RetailChaseCamera.cs: the heading is recomputed from playerYaw on every Update (ComputeHeading at the start of Update, `headingYaw = playerYaw + YawOffset`); the boom is then lerped with ComputeDampingAlpha(0.45, dt). There is no movement gate.
findings.holt_evidence: camera.js:1110-1126 _isPlayerDriving() is true only if the XY position moved (`moved = dx*dx + dy*dy > ...`, :1119) or a WASDQE key is held (:1125). picking.js:857 turnToFaceThenAct turns via `sessionHandle.setMovementInput(0, 0, gate.turn, false)` with no key held and no translation; the same holds for loop.js server turns through turnToHeading. camera.js:244 AUTOFOLLOW_RATE_DEFAULT = 4.0.
findings.discrepancy: When the character turns in place to face a target (melee or cast turn-to-face, a server TurnTo, a wasm pursuit turn), holtburger's camera stays where it was, so the player ends up facing sideways or toward the camera. In retail the camera swings around behind the character with the turn. The ease rate (4.0/s) is also slightly off retail's 10 x 0.45 = 4.5/s.
findings.proposed_change: Track `_lastFollowHeading` in _isPlayerDriving. Return true when |wrapAngle(h - _lastFollowHeading)| > 1e-3 rad since the last frame, using the heading already read by _playerHeadingForFollow; pass it in to avoid a second pose read. This keeps the owner's 'idle holds the camera' behaviour for a truly idle character. Set AUTOFOLLOW_RATE_DEFAULT to 4.5 (and the Camera-tab default autoFollowRate in ui/camera_settings.js) to match retail stiffness 0.45. Extract the decision as a pure `followDrivingNow({moved, keyed, headingDelta})` in camera_math.js.
findings.test_plan: node apps/holtburger-web/tests/camera_retail_math.test.cjs. Pure cases: followDrivingNow({moved:false, keyed:false, headingDelta:0.3}) is true; headingDelta 5e-4 is false; a delta across +/-pi is wrapped. Static assertion that _isPlayerDriving calls followDrivingNow, and that AUTOFOLLOW_RATE_DEFAULT is 4.5.

findings.title: No slope alignment: retail tilts the camera's heading frame to the contact plane (m_bAlignCameraToSlope, default on); holtburger's boom and look direction are always horizontal
findings.decomp_evidence: CameraManager ctor acclient.c:147920 sets `m_bAlignCameraToSlope = 1`. SetTargetForOffset :148214 sets ALIGN_WITH_PLANE for the default offset (|x| <= 1, y <= 0) and always for in-head. CameraManager::UpdateCamera :147604-147700 runs `if (m_bAlignCameraToSlope && target_status & 0x10)`: it pushes the player velocity into a 5-entry ring (old_velocities) and averages it. If |avg.x| and |avg.y| >= 0.0002, the plane normal is the contact-plane normal when the player is in contact (state & 1), otherwise set_vector_heading((v.x, v.y, 0.1*v.z)). The player forward is projected onto that plane to give pivot_direction, so viewer_offset and the LOOK_IN_DIRECTION view pitch up when running uphill and down when running downhill.
findings.openac_evidence: RetailChaseCamera.cs:108-117 (alignmentApplies gate, PushVelocity) and ComputeHeading (projection onto the contact plane, airborne 0.1*vz plane, 2e-4 floors), plus IsOrbitWithinAlignmentThreshold. Tests: RetailChaseCameraTests.cs:136 Heading_OnUphillSlope_TiltsWithSlope, :155 Heading_AirborneJumpingStraightUp_StaysHorizontal, :1122 Orbit_JustPastAlignmentThreshold_DoesNotTilt.
findings.holt_evidence: camera.js:1291-1292 `const forwardX = Math.sin(this.followYaw); const forwardY = Math.cos(this.followYaw);` gives a purely horizontal basis. The ideal eye adds vertical only through pitch (:1297-1304). LocalPlayerPose (lib.rs:34569-34586) exposes x, y, z, heading, landblock_id and on_ground, but no velocity and no contact-plane normal, so JS cannot tilt today.
findings.discrepancy: Retail's chase camera tilts with the slope while moving, which is a characteristic retail feel on hills; holtburger's stays level. It applies only while the player moves with a non-axis-aligned velocity and the boom is within 1 m of directly behind.
findings.proposed_change: Add velocity_x/y/z and contact_normal_x/y/z (plus in_contact) to LocalPlayerPose in lib.rs, filled from the integrator body's velocity and contact plane. In camera_math.js, port OpenAC ComputeHeading, PushVelocity/AverageVelocity (5-ring) and the alignment threshold as pure functions. In positionCamera, build the boom and look offset in the tilted (forward, right, up) basis when alignment applies (not in-head, side offset <= 1 m), with the ring advancing only on aligned frames as in retail. Gate it behind a default-on flag `?camSlopeAlign=off` for A/B.
findings.test_plan: node apps/holtburger-web/tests/camera_retail_math.test.cjs. Port the OpenAC heading cases as pure tests: stationary falls back to yaw; flat ground stays horizontal; an uphill normal (0,-0.5,0.866) with diagonal velocity tilts the forward z positive; an exactly axis-aligned velocity does not tilt (the 2e-4 component floor); jumping straight up stays horizontal; the ring averages the last 5 and evicts FIFO. The wasm pose fields need a rebuild, done by the orchestrator.

areas.area: Audio behaviour (sound tables, ambient scheduling, voice pool)
areas.summary: I compared holtburger-web's audio code with OpenAC's audio code and with the retail decomp. On the holtburger side that was scene3d/audio/*, the hook and PlayEffect sound arms in entities.js, play_effect_vfx.js, the 0xF750 handler in app/client_events.js, plugins/audio_optimistic.js and ui_click_sounds.js, and the event-bake ambient.rs. On the OpenAC side it was Core/Audio/*, the App EntityEffectController and PhysicsScriptRunner, and the tests. In the decomp I checked SoundManager::*, the Ambient/IntermitSound/ConstantSound functions, the Sound/SoundTweaked/SoundTable hook Execute and UnPack functions, ScriptManager, and the CObjectMaint null-object queue. The core rules match retail: the SoundTable row pick (uniform pick of floor((N-1)*roll)) and the separate row-probability roll, the volume and slider-twice rules, SoundTweaked prob@4/prio@8, the 16-voice pool where priority is always 0, GetAttenuation, the inactive-app gate, and the whole ambient model (weights, directions, shares, cadence, queue). Two items in the PARITY-STATUS audio 'open' list are stale: the queued server-sound deadline was fixed in 3133629c and the castVfxDedup silent-copy bug in c5cf6e1a. I also checked the Setup default_sound_table fallback in resolve_sound_table_did. It is not retail, because set_description clears the table, but scanning the DATs shows it has zero practical effect, so I did not report it. The per-wave voice cap (4, default on) is a deliberate Bug-8 departure from retail and I left it alone. The remaining gaps are mostly at the edges: optimistic inventory sounds that play early and then again when the server's sound arrives; sounds on wielded items placed at hand-local coordinates, so they are culled and never heard; a pre-create queue split away from retail's single null-object queue; wire PlayScripts that are not serialized per owner; and a small per-play allocation cost in the SoundTable lookup.

findings.title: Optimistic pickup/drop/wield sounds play at click time AND again when ACE's real 0xF750 arrives (300 ms echo window is shorter than ACE's move-to + pickup-animation delay)
findings.decomp_evidence: Retail has no client-predicted inventory sounds. The only client callers of SoundManager::PlaySoundA are SmartBox::HandleSoundEvent (acclient.c:143333-143350) -> CPhysicsObj::play_sound (316424-316434) -> PlaySoundA(stype, obj, volume) (383655-383678), plus the hook Execute functions (SoundHook/SoundTweakedHook/SoundTableHook::Execute 342188-342221). So in retail the pickup/drop/wield sound plays only when the server's Sound message arrives, i.e. when the action actually happens. ACE cross-check (external/ACE Player_Inventory.cs): a ground pickup sends GameMessageSound(Guid, Sound.PickUpItem) only inside pickupChain.AddAction after the MoveTo + AddPickupChainToMoveToChain (line 1089). Drop runs StartPickupChain (640-658: EnqueueBroadcastMotion(Pickup); pickupChain.AddDelaySeconds(pickupAnimationLength)) and then sends Sound.DropItem (line 1445). Rejections send InventoryServerSaveFailed with no sound.
findings.openac_evidence: OpenAC updates the item table optimistically (Core/Items/ClientObjectTable.cs:447 MoveItemOptimistic, :480 WieldItemOptimistic), but sound comes only from the server SoundEvent: App/Rendering/Vfx/EntityEffectController.cs:90-108 HandleSound -> PlayServerSound (336). No client-predicted cue.
findings.holt_evidence: plugins/audio_optimistic.js:169 playOptimistic plays the player's SoundTable row at click time ({ gain: 1.0 } at :223) and records a suppression claim with `const TTL_MS = 300;` (:130). shouldSuppressEcho (:150-162) returns false once `now > expires` (:155), so a later echo plays. Call sites: plugins/item_drag.js:627 `if (!s?.owned) sfx(0x8F, guid);` (ground or chest pickup), :665 sfx(0x8C) wield, :683 sfx(0x90) drop; plugins/radial-menu.js:364/373 (0x8C), 391 (0x8D), 425/430/462 (0x90 drop / split-to-3D); plugins/inventory.js:763 (0x8D). Echo check: app/client_events.js:1995 `if (window.__audioOptimistic?.shouldSuppressEcho?.(sndEnum, sndGuid))`.
findings.discrepancy: For any pickup from the ground or a container, any drop, and any wield that needs a move-to, ACE's sound arrives after the walk and the pickup animation, which is far longer than the 300 ms TTL. The player therefore hears the sound twice: once at the click, before walking and bending down, and once at the real moment. With round-trip latency over 300 ms, every inventory sound doubles. When the server rejects the action (too far, encumbered, already taken), the player hears a pickup/drop sound for something that never happened. Retail plays exactly one sound, in step with the server's action.
findings.proposed_change: Stop predicting server-echoed sounds. In plugins/audio_optimistic.js add `const OPTIMISTIC_ON = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('audioOptimistic') === 'on'` (opt-in only, because retail parity is the default). In playOptimistic, return early when `!UI_SOUNDS.has(soundId) && !OPTIMISTIC_ON`, so 0x8C/0x8D/0x8E/0x8F/0x90 are left to the 0xF750 handler. The UI-only cues (0x6D UI_GeneralError, 0x73/0x74 slider) keep playing through playUiSound because the server never echoes them. Leave shouldSuppressEcho as is (with no claims recorded it always returns false). Optionally delete the sfx(...) calls in item_drag.js, radial-menu.js and inventory.js to make the intent explicit. Document the flag in docs/url-flags.md.
findings.test_plan: Extend apps/holtburger-web/test_audio_optimistic.mjs (`node test_audio_optimistic.mjs` from apps/holtburger-web). (1) With the default location.search, playOptimistic(0x8F) and playOptimistic(0x90) make no audioManager.play call, and shouldSuppressEcho(0x8F, LPG) returns false right afterwards, so the server's 0xF750 plays exactly once. (2) playOptimistic(0x6D/0x73/0x74) still reaches playFromCenter. (3) With location.search='?audioOptimistic=on', the old behaviour (play plus a 300 ms claim) is unchanged. Before the fix, a scripted 'optimistic fire, then echo at +1200 ms' produces 2 plays; after it, 1.
findings.already_tracked: no (audio_optimistic.js is in the audio facet's file list, but no open item covers the timing or the double play)

findings.title: Sounds on wielded (attached) items use the hand-local root.position, so a weapon/shield/wand buff 'landing' sound is placed near the world origin and culled (silent)
findings.decomp_evidence: CPhysicsObj::set_parent (acclient.c:322952-) calls change_cell(child, parent->cell) and then CPhysicsObj::UpdateChild. UpdateChild (320039-320056) does Frame::combine(&new_frame, &parts[part_index]->pos.frame, child_frame) and set_frame(child_obj, &new_frame), so the child's m_position is a WORLD frame, and then runs ScriptManager::UpdateScripts(child_obj->script_manager). CPhysicsObj::play_script(PScriptType) (320326-) needs this->cell (set by set_parent) and queues the script on the child's own ScriptManager. Its SoundTableHook::Execute -> PlaySoundA(stype, physobj) (342219-342221, 383681-383703) plays at &physobj->m_position using the child's own sound_table. ACE WorldObject_Magic.cs:361-365 DoSpellEffects broadcasts GameMessageScript(target.Guid, spell.TargetEffect) with target = the wielded item. DAT check (portal.dat, my python btree reader): the weapon PhysicsScriptTable 0x3400002B, used by every melee/missile/caster weenie in LSD, has 16 of 17 first scripts containing a SoundTable(2) hook at t=0 (e.g. key 0x39 -> 0x330000EE hooks [13,2,13]).
findings.openac_evidence: OpenAC places script and server sounds at the owner's ROOT WORLD pose: App/Rendering/Vfx/EntityEffectController.cs:336-344 PlaySoundServerSound uses `_poses.TryGetRootPose(ownerLocalId, out Matrix4x4 rootWorld) ? rootWorld.Translation : Vector3.Zero`, and :541-544 refreshes PhysicsScriptRunner owner anchors the same way (Core/Vfx/PhysicsScriptRunner.cs:56 SetOwnerAnchor, :269 dispatch uses the anchor).
findings.holt_evidence: Attach reparents the child under the wielder's part: scene3d/entities.js:6698 `mount.add(c.root);` and :6717 `c.root.position.set(loc.ox, loc.oy, loc.oz);`, so root.position becomes a hand-local offset. Every sound site still reads the raw root.position as if it were global AC metres: _fireHook (16374) `const pos = inst.root.position;` (16416) -> Sound(1) `acToThree(pos.x,pos.y,pos.z)` (16451); SoundTable(2) `const px = inst.root.position.x;` (16533); SoundTweaked(21) `acToThree(pos.x, pos.y, pos.z)` (16772); _firePlayEffectSoundHook (13683) `const pos = rig?.position ?? {x:0,y:0,z:0};` (13706); app/client_events.js:1950 `const pos = inst.root?.position;` (0xF750); follow-mode lookup in scene3d/index.js:2500 `const p = inst?.root?.position;`. Wire PlayEffect sounds reach the child through play_effect_vfx.js:2453 `em._firePlayEffectSoundHook(targetGuid >>> 0, desc)`. In audio_manager.js _playHrtf, retailAttenuation(dist ~ tens of km) gives play:false, so the sound is skipped.
findings.discrepancy: Retail plays a wielded item's script and sound hooks (item-enchant TargetEffect chimes, SoundTable hooks, server sounds on the item guid) at the item's world position, i.e. at the player's hand. Holtburger places them at the hand-local offset (about (0.05, 0, 0.1)), interpreted as global coordinates, which is near (0,0,0) and thousands of metres from the listener. They are culled at -50 dB and never heard. The follow-mode panner update has the same bug.
findings.proposed_change: Add a pure helper module scene3d/audio/emitter_position.js: `export function emitterPosThree(inst, scratchV3)`. It returns null without inst.root. When `inst._attachedParentGuid != null` (or `inst.root.userData.__attachedChildOf`), it returns `inst.root.getWorldPosition(scratchV3)` copied to {x,y,z}; this is already in the three.js listener frame because worldRoot's -pi/2 rotation and the hand part transform are both included. Otherwise it returns acToThree(root.position). Use it instead of `acToThree(inst.root.position...)` in entities.js _fireHook (Sound 1, SoundTable 2 at resolve time, SoundTweaked 21), _firePlayEffectSoundHook (ht 1/21; ht 2 goes through _fireHook), the legacy ?scriptQueue=off walker arm (rig.position), app/client_events.js runServerSound, and the scene3d/index.js updateFollowingPositions lookup. Keep the AC-frame world_pos in event-log records by converting back with threeToAc from retail_mixer.js. Related render issue, not part of this audio fix: play_effect_vfx.js:797-818 _resolveTargetPlacement uses inst.root.position too, so placeholder bursts on wielded items land at the origin.
findings.test_plan: New tests/audio_attached_emitter.test.mjs (`node tests/audio_attached_emitter.test.mjs`; three.js is already imported by tests such as tests/projectile_spin.test.mjs). Build worldRoot (rotation.x=-PI/2) -> entitiesGroup -> parent root at AC (32450, 28010, 60) -> part node at (0,0,1.2) -> child root at local (0.05,0,0.1) with inst._attachedParentGuid set. Assert emitterPosThree(child) is within 0.5 m of acToThree(32450.05, 28010, 61.3). Assert emitterPosThree(topLevel) equals acToThree(root.position) exactly, so non-attached entities are unchanged. Assert retail_mixer getAttenuation(distance(listener at the parent, helper result), 1, 1).play === true, while the old raw-local path gives play === false.

findings.title: Pre-create queues are split: PlayScripts (and the sound hooks inside them) expire 3 s per entry, server sounds 25 s sliding, attach/visibility in a third buffer, and drain order is by kind rather than arrival
findings.decomp_evidence: SmartBox::HandleSoundEvent (acclient.c:143333-143350), HandlePlayScriptID (143354-143372) and HandlePlayScriptType (143375-143393) all call CObjectMaint::QueueBlobForObject for an unknown guid. QueueBlobForObject (310848-310861) puts every blob kind on ONE null object (GetNullObject(id,1)) via CPhysicsObj::queue_netblob (a single FIFO). AddObjectToBeDestroyed (310650-310672) re-arms that one null object's destruction at cur_time + 25.0 on every queued blob. When the object is created, the blobs replay in arrival order.
findings.openac_evidence: App/Rendering/Vfx/EntityEffectController.cs:105/108 (Sound) and :128 (Typed PlayScript) both call one `Enqueue(serverGuid, PendingEffect)` (a single Queue<PendingEffect> per guid, ~547-555). TryReplayPending (558-568) replays the whole queue FIFO through Execute (Direct / Typed / Sound).
findings.holt_evidence: PlayEffects for unknown guids use their own queue with `const _PENDING_TTL_MS = 3000;` per entry (scene3d/play_effect_vfx.js:3199, pruned per entry at 3245), capped at 8 per guid and 256 guids. Server sounds use PendingObjectSounds with a 25 s sliding deadline (scene3d/audio/retail_sound_rules.js OBJECT_BLOB_TTL_S). Attach and visibility use the generic `this._preCreate` buffer (scene3d/pre_create_buffer.js, 25 s sliding). On spawn the drains run in fixed kind order: entities.js:5242 drainPendingPlayEffects, :5244 drainPendingObjectSounds, then :5331 this._drainPreCreate(guid). So a wielded child's queued effect or sound replays before its parked attach is applied.
findings.discrepancy: In retail, a PlayScript that arrives 4-25 s before its object (or that is kept alive by a later sound or effect blob) still plays, including its sound hooks, and all blobs replay in arrival order. Holtburger drops script effects and their sounds after 3 s even while a later sound keeps the guid alive. It also replays PlayEffects and sounds before a parked ParentEvent, so effects on a just-created wielded item play at its pre-attach pose.
findings.proposed_change: Route both kinds into the generic buffer that already has retail semantics. In play_effect_vfx.js, at the missing-target enqueue site, call `em._preCreate.enqueue(guid, 'playEffect', {scriptId, speed, silent, ...})` when `em._preCreateBufferOn`. In app/client_events.js runServerSound's !inst branch, call `emgr._preCreate.enqueue(sndGuid, 'sound', {replay})` instead of pendingObjectSounds.add. In entities.js _drainPreCreate, handle 'playEffect' (call the existing replay function used by drainPendingPlayEffects) and 'sound' (call replay()) in FIFO order alongside attach/visibility. Move the drainPendingPlayEffects/drainPendingObjectSounds calls at 5242-5244 into the ?preCreateBuffer=off arm only. Keep the old queues as the off-path.
findings.test_plan: Extend the existing pure test for scene3d/pre_create_buffer.js, or add tests/pre_create_mixed_kinds.test.mjs using createPreCreateBuffer({now}): enqueue playEffect at t=0, sound at t=20 s, attach at t=21 s; at t=30 s takeFor(guid) returns all three in arrival order; at t=46.001 s the bucket has expired. Add an arm to tests/audio_server_sound.test.mjs asserting that a 0xF750 for an unknown guid goes into the generic buffer and replays once on drain.
findings.already_tracked: partly: the PARITY-STATUS audio open item about the 25 s sliding deadline was fixed for server sounds only (3133629c); the 3 s PlayEffect TTL and the cross-kind order are not tracked

findings.title: Wire PlayScripts (and their sound hooks) are not serialized on the owner's ScriptManager, so back-to-back scripts on one object overlap instead of queueing
findings.decomp_evidence: CPhysicsObj::play_script(PScriptType) (acclient.c:320326-) -> play_script_internal -> ScriptManager::AddScript -> AddScriptInternal (329069-): `if (last_data) start = last_data->script->length + last_data->start_time; else start = cur_time`. ScriptManager::UpdateScripts (329189-) / NextHook fire hooks at script.start_time + hook.start_time and move on to the next script only after the current one finishes. CallPES with a pause uses an FPHook and then the same play_script_internal path (318973-319005).
findings.openac_evidence: Core/Vfx/PhysicsScriptRunner.cs:90-92 `double start = owner.Scripts.Count == 0 ? _clock() : owner.Scripts[^1].StartTime + owner.Scripts[^1].Duration;`. Direct and typed wire PlayScripts both go through PlayDirect (63) / Play (129).
findings.holt_evidence: Entity-spawn and CallPES scripts use the owner queue (entities.js _queuePhysicsScript ~14071, default-on ?scriptQueue). The wire PlayEffect path does not: play_effect_vfx.js:2423-2453 decodes the script's Sound/SoundTable/SoundTweaked hooks and calls em._firePlayEffectSoundHook immediately; that function (entities.js:13683) schedules each one with setTimeout(startTime) from receipt, with no reference to the owner's ScriptManager.
findings.discrepancy: In retail, a second PlayScript on the same object (rapid buff casts on one target, several debuffs landing together, a hit effect on a creature running a looping default script) starts after the earlier script's length, so its sound follows the first one. Holtburger starts every wire script at receipt, so the cues overlap and stack. This also bypasses the despawn cleanup that the owner's ScriptManager gets.
findings.proposed_change: In play_effect_vfx.js, after resolving the PES entries for a live target and once the dedup/synthetic-caster bookkeeping is done, hand the entries to `em._queuePhysicsScript(targetGuid, inst.root, pesId, entries)` when SCRIPT_QUEUE_ON, instead of firing sound hooks directly through _firePlayEffectSoundHook. Particle hooks would then also go through _executeScriptHook. Keep the soundOnly / silent dedup modes by filtering entries before queueing. Behaviour change for VFX timing too, so coordinate with the particles_vfx facet owner.
findings.test_plan: Add an arm to apps/holtburger-web/tests/test_ws09_play_effect_sound.mjs (or the existing script-queue test): two wire PlayEffects on the same guid, 50 ms apart, with a fake script of length 1.0 s containing a t=0 SoundTable hook. Assert the second sound fires at ~1.0 s after the first (fake clock), not at +50 ms. Assert a despawn between them cancels the second sound.

findings.title: SoundTableCache.resolveSound crosses the wasm boundary and allocates/frees N SoundEntryJs handles on every play (footsteps, server sounds, UI clicks)
findings.decomp_evidence: Retail SoundManager::GetSound (acclient.c:383433-383463) is a hash lookup into the resident CSoundTable (CSoundTable::Lookup 385195 -> SoundTableData::Lookup) that copies 4 fields into a stack SoundData. There is no per-play allocation.
findings.openac_evidence: Core/Audio/SoundCookbook.cs:42-47 Select(table, sound, rng) indexes the already-parsed table.Sounds[sound].Entries list directly; PickVariant (11-23) allocates nothing.
findings.holt_evidence: scene3d/audio/sound_table_cache.js:212 resolveSound calls `entries = stb.entriesForSound(enumU32);` (219) on every call, snapshots one entry, then frees every wasm handle (`e.free()`, 262). The wasm side, apps/holtburger-web/src/lib.rs:46094-46100 entries_for_sound, does `Some(v) => v.clone()`, i.e. a fresh Vec<SoundEntryJs> and N wasm-bindgen wrapper objects each time.
findings.discrepancy: Every sound event pays a wasm call, N wrapper allocations and N frees (each going through FinalizationRegistry bookkeeping) for data that never changes. With many walking creatures this means hundreds of allocations per second on the main thread for nothing.
findings.proposed_change: Memoize plain rows per (did, soundEnum) in SoundTableCache. Add `this._rows = new Map()` keyed by `did * 0x10000 + enum` (or a nested Map) holding a frozen array of {waveDid, priority, probability, volume} POJOs, built once from entriesForSound and the handles freed right away. resolveSound then does the same uniform `Math.floor((rows.length-1) * this._rng())` pick on the cached array and returns the POJO, or a shallow copy if callers mutate it. Clear _rows in dispose(). Note: the JSDoc at lib.rs:46091-46093 still describes the old 'probability-weighted' pick; fix that comment when lib.rs is next touched (no rebuild needed for this change).
findings.test_plan: New tests/audio_sound_table_cache.test.mjs (there is currently no test for this module). Use a fake fetchSoundTable whose entriesForSound counts calls and returns objects with free(). (1) 100 resolveSound(did, 0x37) calls invoke entriesForSound once. (2) The pick is uniform floor((N-1)*r): with N=2, r=0.999 still returns entry 0 (retail quirk, OpenAC SoundCookbookTests PickVariant_TwoEntries_LastIsUnreachable); with N=3, r=0.5 returns entry 1. (3) Every handle's free() was called exactly once. (4) dispose() clears the row cache.

areas.area: Dereth calendar, time of day and day-group/weather selection (behaviour only)
areas.summary:
I compared OpenAC's DerethCalendar, DerethDateTime, SkyDayGroupSelector, WorldTimeService (SkyState.cs), WeatherState and RuntimeWorldEnvironmentState against holtburger's sky.rs evaluator, the wasm glue in lib.rs, the TimeSync path, map-panel.js, daygroup_weather.js, weather_state.js and atmosphere_sky.js. The authority was the retail decomp: GameTime::UseTime, CalcDayBegin, CalcTimeOfDay, GetDateTimeString, SkyDesc::CalcPresentDayGroup (acclient.c and the Binary Ninja pseudo-C), Timer::set_time, ClientNet::HandleTimeSynch and gmMapUI. I also checked ACE's Timers.PortalYearTicks and DerethDateTime.

**What holtburger gets right.** Its calendar arithmetic matches retail: zero_time_of_year 3600, year/day split, and the 1782775218/1967253934 day-group hash done in f64. That is closer to retail's x87 computation than OpenAC's float path. One tiny gap: holtburger uses the decimal literal 2.3283064e-10 where the binary has 2.32830644e-10f, which is exactly 2^-32. The relative error is 1.6e-8, so a day picks a different group with probability of roughly 1e-7. It is not worth a change; if the code is touched anyway, `(h as u64 * n) >> 32` would be bit-exact.

**Main defect: the clock.** The sky's time of day and its DayGroup run on a private wall clock anchored at 1999-11-02 UTC. Retail and ACE use the server's TimeSync clock (PortalYearTicks). As a result:
- holtburger's sky runs 780 s ahead (about 1.6 of the 16 named hours).
- It is on a completely different calendar day, so it shows a different DayGroup (weather) than every retail client on the same server.
- It also disagrees with holtburger's own map panel, which already reads the server clock.

**Secondary issues.**
- The weather profile is chosen by DayGroup index from a made-up 20-entry table. The DAT has only Sunny, Clear, Cloudy and Rainy, so a Sunny day can be given a snow profile. The season is also fixed at spring. Fixing either of these changes rendering.
- The date/time strings and hour/month lookup are hardcoded in JS instead of ported from the Region GameTime tables.

**Considered and rejected.**
- Forward-only TimeSync: retail's Timer::set_time ignores server samples that don't move the clock forward, but the gain is small and it could interact with ACE's echo speed-hack check.
- AdminEnvirons: already handled in misc.rs.
- Per-frame sky evaluation cost: already consolidated to one call per frame.

None of these is tracked in PARITY-STATUS.json.

findings.title: Sky time of day and DayGroup run on a private 1999-anchored wall clock instead of the server PortalYearTicks clock (retail Timer::cur_time); 780 s ahead and on a different day than retail and the client's own map panel
findings.decomp_evidence: GameTime::UseTime (acclient.c:463395-463416): `time = Timer::cur_time + this->clock_offset + this->time_zero_start_delta`; clock_offset is only ever zeroed (463386, 463475) and time_zero_start_delta = GameSky::s_timeAdjustment, a debug knob (308547). GameTime::CalcDayBegin (463203-463240): `total_time = time + zero_time_of_year; current_year = zero_year + floor(total/year_length); current_day = floor(offset_in_year/day_length)`. present_time_of_day = (time - time_of_day_begin)/day_length. Timer::cur_time IS the server clock: ClientNet::HandleTimeSynch (371516-371533) calls `Timer::set_time(&srvtime)`, and Timer::set_time (75365-75407) writes `Timer::cur_time = m_tExternalTime = srvtime`. SkyDesc::CalcPresentDayGroup (301664-301690) hashes `current_day + days_per_year*current_year` from GameTime, so the weather of the day is a pure function of server time. Server side: ACE sends Timers.PortalYearTicks in TimeSync and ConnectRequest (NetworkSession.cs:938, AuthenticationHandler.cs:119). That value starts at DerethDateTime.UtcNowToEMUTime = (UtcNow-5h) - 2017-01-31 12:00 (DerethDateTime.cs:1062), then accumulates per loop (WorldManager.cs:391), so it can drift from wall time.
findings.openac_evidence: SkyState.cs:232-264: WorldTimeService.SyncFromServer(serverTicks) stores the ticks, and NowTicks = _lastSyncedTicks + elapsed*TickSize. DayFraction is Calendar.DayFraction(NowTicks). WorldSession.cs:1186-1192 raises TimeSync as ServerTimeUpdated, and WorldSession.Connection.cs:144-145 seeds it from the ConnectRequest time. RuntimeWorldEnvironmentState.cs:176 installs the Region origin (`WorldTime.Calendar.SetOriginOffset(definition.OriginOffsetTicks)`). Its :195-200 SynchronizeFromServer calls RefreshDayGroup, which picks the group from server ticks (:240-270). DerethDateTimeTests.cs:91-98 pins origin 3600: tick 291,408,060 is Seedsow 24, 116 P.Y.
findings.holt_evidence: crates/holtburger-world/src/sky.rs:62 `pub const AC_LAUNCH_UNIX_EPOCH: f64 = 941_500_800.0;`. :366 Default is `Self::new_with_anchor_unix(AC_LAUNCH_UNIX_EPOCH)`. :432-434 `(now_unix - self.anchor_unix) + game_time.zero_time_of_year`. :572-574 game_time_dpy hardcodes `360` instead of GameTime.days_per_year. apps/holtburger-web/src/lib.rs:20122 `let now_unix = js_date_now_ms() / 1000.0;` feeds evaluate(); :19704 builds `SkyEvalState::new()` with no server clock. src/session/messages/mod.rs:91-97 sends TimeSync only to WorldState::set_server_time_sync, never to the sky. scene3d/atmosphere_sky.js:46 and :64-69 apply the same 1999 anchor to the moon and stars. Meanwhile plugins/map-panel.js:646-647 builds its date from `handle.serverTime()` (the PortalYearTicks domain), and map-panel.js:324-337 adds ZERO_TIME_OF_YEAR 3600. docs/url-flags.md:923 documents the default as 'wall-clock UTC'.
findings.discrepancy: holtburger computes world seconds as now-941500800+3600, while retail and ACE use PortalYearTicks+3600 with PortalYearTicks ≈ now-1485882000. The two differ by 544,381,200 s, which is ≡ 780 s (mod 7620). So the holtburger sky is 780 s, or 0.102 of a day (about 1.6 of the 16 named hours), ahead of retail. The calendar day is also completely different. On 2026-10-08 holtburger is in year 319, day 305, while the server is in year 121 P.Y., day 144. Different (day, year) seeds give a different DayGroup (Sunny/Rainy) than every retail client on the same server. The client's own map panel can say 'Time: Foredawn' while its sky shows Dawnsong. The sky also never follows ACE's accumulated clock drift.
findings.proposed_change: 1) sky.rs: add `pub const ACE_EMU_EPOCH_UNIX: f64 = 1_485_882_000.0;` (2017-01-31 17:00 UTC, the ACE UtcNowToEMUTime zero). Make Default use it in place of AC_LAUNCH_UNIX_EPOCH. Add `pub fn set_server_clock(&mut self, portal_ticks: f64, at_unix: f64) { self.anchor_unix = at_unix - portal_ticks; self.cached_day_group = None; }`. world_time_seconds then equals PortalYearTicks + zero_time_of_year, which is retail CalcDayBegin's total_time. Keeping the anchor_unix model means the existing new_with_anchor_unix tests stay valid. Pass game_time.days_per_year into select_day_group and delete game_time_dpy (it hardcodes 360). Leave session_start_unix/tex scroll on now_unix so a sync never jumps cloud UVs. 2) lib.rs: add thread_local `SKY_SERVER_CLOCK: Cell<Option<(f64,f64)>>` and `fn note_sky_server_time(t)`. It stores (t, js_date_now_ms()/1000) and calls evaluator.set_server_clock on SKY_SHADOW if it is populated. populate_sky_desc_from_region (~:19697-19706) seeds the new evaluator from the stash. Call note_sky_server_time in the session/messages/mod.rs TimeSync arm, next to set_server_time_sync. A day's weather identity is the DayGroup record itself: its day_name plus its sky objects. chance_of_occur is never read. Region 0x13000000 has only four day_name values, Sunny/Clear/Cloudy/Rainy (docs/dat-patch/research/sky-holtburger-quality-plan.md:64-68, region-export-json: Sunny x5, Clear x3, Cloudy x4, Rainy x8). docs/3d-port-state-2026-05-10.md:80 lists the same four names with a different, internally inconsistent count; sky.rs:1448 notes DayGroup[0] is 'Sunny'. GameTime has 12 seasons (the months; CalcDayBegin sets current_season at :463238), so Dereth does have calendar seasons.
findings.openac_evidence: WeatherState.cs:77-96 SetKindFromDayGroupName maps the lower-cased DayGroup name by keyword (rain/cloud/snow/storm/fog → Overcast, else Clear). RuntimeWorldEnvironmentState.cs:270 calls `Weather.SetKindFromDayGroupName(group.Name)` whenever the day group changes.
findings.holt_evidence: scene3d/daygroup_weather.js:16-19 says 'Order is INFERRED — retail order isn't formally documented'. :25-66 PROFILES[0..19] includes light-snow(8) -1°C, heavy-snow(9) -5°C, hot-dry(12) 32°C, cold-clear(13) 2°C and hail(19). :179-185 weatherForState uses `PROFILES[dayGroupIndex]`. scene3d/loop.js:1454 calls `weatherForState(state, state.dayGroupIndex, skyObjects)`. scene3d/weather_state.js:78 `season: 1` is never derived; PROFILES carry no season, so :241 never updates it. vfx/weather_inputs.js:85-89 frostTarget(tempC, season) is driven by these values. vfx/particle_env.js:65 claims 'Dereth has no calendar autumn'. findings.discrepancy: A Sunny or Clear DAT day that lands on index 8, 9 or 13 gets -1 to -5°C, so the frost target is about 1 and the cloud base sits low on a clear day. A Rainy day on index 12 gets 32°C hot-dry. is_storm already comes from real sky objects (W4), but temperature, dewpoint and pressure still come from a fabricated index mapping. Season-gated particles (pollen, fireflies, leaves) always run as spring, whatever the Dereth month.

findings.decomp_evidence: GameTime::CalcTimeOfDay (acclient.c:463243-463282) sets current_time_of_day by bracketing times_of_day[i]->begin (stored at :463270). GameTime::CalcDayBegin (463203-463240) sets current_season by bracketing seasons[i]->begin (:463238). GameTime::GetDateTimeString (463286-463349) builds the time from times_of_day[t].name and formats the date with `_sprintf(date_string, "%s %s, %s %s", season_name, day - season->begin + 1, year, year_spec)` (:463349). gmMapUI prefixes 'Date: '/'Time: ' and refreshes every 5 s (`m_nextUpdate = Timer::cur_time + 5.0`, :218474).

findings.holt_evidence: plugins/map-panel.js:302-337 hardcodes DAY_TICKS 7620, ZERO_TIME_OF_YEAR 3600, ZERO_YEAR 10, 360-day years and 30-day months, `hourIndex = Math.min(15, Math.floor(timeOfDay * 16))`, the DERETH_MONTHS/DERETH_HOURS name lists, and the literal ' P.Y.'. It agrees with retail only as long as the DAT holds 16 uniform slots and 12 thirty-day seasons with exactly these strings. A patched or custom Region (the planned DAT-patched sky work) would show wrong names or boundaries. A season index for daytime-2 is also not available.
findings.proposed_change: Add a pure port to holtburger-world (sky.rs or a new game_time_eval.rs): `pub fn dereth_calendar(gt: &GameTime, portal_ticks: f64) -> DerethCalendarSnapshot { year, day_of_year, season_index, day_in_season, time_of_day_index, present_time_of_day, date_string, time_string }`. It mirrors CalcDayBegin (total = ticks + zero_time_of_year; year = zero_year + floor(total/(day_length*days_per_year)); season = last seasons[i].start <= day), CalcTimeOfDay (bracket times_of_day[i].start) and GetDateTimeString (`format!("{} {}, {} {}", season.name, day - season.start + 1, year, year_spec)`). Export it as `getDerethCalendar()` from lib.rs on the same clock as daytime-1. (the same anchors as test_map_panel.mjs:266-282). Add a non-uniform-begins case proving the bracket search, not floor(t*16). areas.area: Chat, channels, emotes and client commands
areas.summary: I compared three things: holtburger-web's chat path (app/slash_commands.js, app/chat_log.js, app/client_events.js, the index.html submit handler, plugins/emote-panel.js, and the wasm arms in src/session/messages/chat.rs, game_event.rs and commands/social.rs); OpenAC's AcDream.Runtime/Core Chat code and tests; and the retail decomp's ClientCommunicationSystem (OnChatCommand, DoCommand, PublicChat/Pose, the Hear* handlers, ChannelBroadcast, the TurbineChat send path, CanHear). I also cross-checked against vanilla ACE in ~/ace-server. The verdict is that holtburger's chat has several real retail divergences that players will notice, and none of them is tracked in PARITY-STATUS or fixed in recent git history. The worst is that every Turbine channel command sends to the wrong room. The JS sends General as 1, but 1 is retail's Allegiance (ChatTypeEnum), so General text goes to the Allegiance room and Trade text goes to General. On top of that, /a uses the legacy Allegiance Broadcast channel, which ACE only allows for Speakers. Other problems: emote lines have no actor name; every message you send appears twice, and the copy from the server is badly worded; '@', ':' and ';' prefixes and most retail aliases are not handled on the client; NPC tells become the /r target; and squelch is never applied on the client, while ACE does not squelch emotes on the server. OpenAC handles most of these well (prefix parsing, inline *pose*, player-only reply targets, retail channel sentences), but it has no client-side squelch filter, so retail is the only reference for that one. All findings change behaviour or HUD text only; none touch rendering.

findings.title: Turbine channel commands send to the wrong room (off-by-one ChatTypeEnum), and /a uses the Speaker-only legacy Allegiance Broadcast
findings.decomp_evidence: acclient.h:4464 `enum ChatTypeEnum { Allegiance_ChatTypeEnum = 0x1, General_ChatTypeEnum = 0x2, Trade = 0x3, LFG = 0x4, Roleplay = 0x5, Society = 0x6, SocietyCelHan 0x7, SocietyEldWeb 0x8, SocietyRadBlo 0x9, Olthoi_ChatTypeEnum = 0xA }`. ClientCommunicationSystem::StartupTurbineChatSystem (acclient.c:424334) registers a/guild/gu -> DoTurbineChat_Allegiance, general/cg, trade/ct, lfg/clfg, roleplay/crp, society/soc, olthoi/o. DoTurbineChat_Allegiance (acclient.c:424053) calls `SendTurbineChat(v4, v7, Allegiance_ChatTypeEnum, ...)` on the allegiance room. InitializeCommands (acclient.c:426432) maps "ab" separately to DoAllegianceBroadcast.
findings.openac_evidence: src/AcDream.Core.Net/Messages/TurbineChat.cs:44-53 `Allegiance = 1, General = 2, Trade = 3 ... Olthoi = 10`. src/AcDream.Runtime/Chat/LiveChatCommandRoute.cs:30-38 TurbineChannelKinds sends Allegiance/General/Trade/Lfg/Roleplay/Society/Olthoi through Turbine chat. At :160-168 it falls back to legacy AllegianceBroadcast only when `!bindings.TurbineChat.Enabled`. ChatInputParser.cs:32-34 has `("/guild", Allegiance)` and `("/ab", AllegianceBroadcast)`.
findings.holt_evidence: app/slash_commands.js:186-191 `TURBINE_CMDS = { cg: { type: 1, label: "General" }, ct: 2, clfg: 3, crp: 4, society: 5, olthoi: { type: 9 } }`, sent at :194 by `handle.sendTurbineChannel(entry.type, rest)`. src/session/commands/social.rs:177 SendTurbineChannel arm decodes with `TurbineChatType::from_repr(chat_type)`, then `channels.channel_for_type(chat_type_enum)`. crates/holtburger-protocol/src/messages/chat/turbine.rs:33-44 defines `Allegiance = 1, General = 2, Trade = 3, Lfg = 4, Roleplay = 5, Society = 6, ... Olthoi = 10`. slash_commands.js:155-156 `a: 0x02000000, // AllegianceBroadcast`. app/chat_log.js:184 the Allegiance talk focus uses prefix "/a ". In ACE GameActionChatChannel.cs, `case Channel.AllegianceBroadcast`: `if (player.AllegiancePermissionLevel < AllegiancePermissionLevel.Speaker) -> YouDoNotHaveAuthorityInAllegiance`. The lib.rs doc comments on SessionCommand::SendTurbineChannel and send_turbine_channel wrongly say "General=1 ... Allegiance=10" (blame shows the enum is unchanged since 2026-05-03, so the JS table was wrong from the start).
findings.discrepancy: /cg resolves to the Allegiance room: members of an allegiance post General text into allegiance chat, everyone else gets a 'not advertised' error. /ct goes to General, /clfg to Trade, /crp to LFG, /society to Roleplay, /olthoi to SocietyRadBlo. /a and the Allegiance talk focus use legacy 0x02000000, which ACE rejects for anyone below Speaker, so ordinary members cannot talk in allegiance chat. Retail @a uses the Turbine Allegiance room; @ab is the separate legacy broadcast.
findings.proposed_change: In app/slash_commands.js, change TURBINE_CMDS to retail ChatTypeEnum values and add the retail aliases: {a,guild,gu:1 'Allegiance'}, {cg,general:2}, {ct,trade:3}, {clfg,lfg:4}, {crp,roleplay:5}, {society,soc:6}, {olthoi,o:10}. Remove `a` from CHANNEL_MAP and add `ab: 0x02000000`. The Allegiance talk focus can keep the "/a " prefix, which now routes to Turbine. Correct the two lib.rs doc comments (doc-only change). Optional, matching OpenAC (this part needs a wasm rebuild): in the social.rs SendTurbineChannel arm, when chat_type==Allegiance and Turbine chat is disabled or no allegiance room is advertised, send GameAction::ChatChannel(0x02000000) instead of returning an error.
findings.test_plan: New apps/holtburger-web/test_slash_commands.mjs (run with `node test_slash_commands.mjs`). Stub `globalThis.window = {}`, import initSlashCommands, and use a fake handle that records sendTurbineChannel/sendChannel/sendChat calls. Assert: `/cg hi` -> sendTurbineChannel(2,'hi'); /ct -> 3; /clfg -> 4; /crp -> 5; /society -> 6; /olthoi -> 10; `/a hi` and `/guild hi` -> sendTurbineChannel(1,'hi'); `/ab hi` -> sendChannel(0x02000000,'hi'). Also check that every TALK_FOCUSES prefix produces a client-side call and never the `@cmd` fall-through. Update the ROUTED set in test_chat_panel_layout.mjs if prefixes change.

findings.title: EmoteText and SoulEmote lines leave out the actor's name; your own SoulEmote echo is not dropped
findings.decomp_evidence: ClientCommunicationSystem::Handle_Communication__HearEmote (acclient.c:422448) builds the line as `name`, then " " unless msg[0]=='\'' (39), then msg + "\n", and calls AddTextToScroll(..., 0xC). Handle_Communication__HearSoulEmote (acclient.c:422716): `if ( sender == v5 /*player_id*/ ) result = 0; else ... HearEmote(...)`, so your own echo is dropped. ClientCommunicationSystem::Pose (acclient.c:425512) shows that otherEmote carries no name: it sends `Event_SoulEmote(&otherEmote)` and echoes locally with `HearSoulEmote(v24, 0, "You", &myEmote)`.
findings.openac_evidence: src/AcDream.Core/Chat/ChatLineWording.cs:74-77 `EmoteLine(entry) => entry.Text.StartsWith('\'') ? $"{entry.Sender}{entry.Text}" : $"{entry.Sender} {entry.Text}"`, used for both ChatKind.Emote and ChatKind.SoulEmote (lines 62-63).
findings.holt_evidence: src/session/messages/chat.rs:98-105 EmoteText arm `string_payload: Some(data.text.clone())`; the comment claims ACE pre-renders "Alice waves at you.". chat.rs:122-128 SoulEmote arm does the same, with no sender==player check. ACE actually sends the raw text: Player.cs:826 `EnqueueBroadcast(new GameMessageEmoteText(Guid.Full, GetNameWithSuffix(), message), ...)` and GameMessageSoulEmote(Guid.Full, Name, message). holtburger's own CLI prepends the name (apps/holtburger-cli/src/pages/game/panels/chat.rs:165-169 `format!("{} {}", sender, text)`), and the holtburger-core test sends text "waves." with sender "Fellow".
findings.discrepancy: In the web client, Bob's `/me waves` appears as "waves" and his *wave* soul emote as "waves.", with no actor named. Your own soul emotes appear twice: the local "You wave." echo plus the server echo. ACE's '^'/'&' Olthoi name suffixes are never stripped.
findings.proposed_change: Add a pure, non-wasm32-gated module apps/holtburger-web/src/chat_format.rs with `strip_name_markers(name)` (trims trailing '^'/'&' like the retail PStringBase::trim calls) and `format_emote_line(name, text)` (no space when text starts with '\''). Use it in the chat.rs EmoteText and SoulEmote arms for the CHAT_RECEIVED string; leave the OVERHEAD_SPEECH bubble payload unchanged. In the SoulEmote arm, also destructure `state` from LoopCtx and skip the CHAT_RECEIVED push when `LoopState::InWorld { player_guid }` matches data.sender (retail HearSoulEmote). Fix the misleading comment.
findings.test_plan: Add Rust #[test]s in src/chat_format.rs: format_emote_line("Bob","waves.")=="Bob waves."; format_emote_line("Bob","'s eyes narrow.")=="Bob's eyes narrow."; format_emote_line("Bob^","waves.")=="Bob waves.". The orchestrator runs `capped-build cargo test -p holtburger-web --lib chat_format` once after merging (agents must not run cargo). After the wasm rebuild, smoke-test in one session: a second account's /me shows "Name waves".

findings.title: Your own chat appears twice: local echoes plus server echoes, and the server copies are badly worded
findings.decomp_evidence: The retail send paths add no local text: DoTell (acclient.c:417964) only calls SetLastTelleeName and Event_TalkDirectByName; DoEmote (418684) only Event_Emote; DoChannelCommand (417344) only Event_ChannelBroadcast; SendTurbineChat (423195) only CSendToTurbineRoomByID; PublicChat (426025) only Event_Talk. Handle_Communication__ChannelBroadcast (412975): an empty senderName gives "[Fellowship] You say, \"" (type 19), "You say to your <chan>, \"" for 0x1000/0x2000/0x4000 (type 11), and "[Co-Vassals]"/"[Allegiance Broadcast] You say" (type 10); heard lines are "Your patron/vassal/follower %s says to you" and "[Fellowship] %s says". findings.holt_evidence: index.html:4851 `appendChatLine(`> ${message}`, null)` after every plain say; its comment says "ACE doesn't echo Talk back", which is false (ACE WorldObject_Networking EnqueueBroadcast does `self.Session.Network.EnqueueSend(msg)` first). slash_commands.js echoes locally at :95 (`You tell ${target}`), :175 (`[${label}] You say`), :200 (`[${label}] ${rest}`) and :222 (`> ${action}`); plugins/emote-panel.js:384 `echo(`> ${text}`)`. chat.rs:36 `format!("[Server] {}", data.message)`; ACE echoes tells as GameMessageSystemChat("You tell X", OutgoingTell), but only when X is online. chat.rs:42 HearSpeech always uses "{} says". game_event.rs:149-165 ChannelBroadcast always uses `[{label}] {sender} says`, and ACE echoes your own channel line with sender "". findings.title: Command input misses retail prefixes and aliases: '@' bypasses client verbs, ':'/';' emote shortcuts, verb aliases, inline *pose* tokens, and %p gender
findings.decomp_evidence: ClientCommunicationSystem::OnChatCommand (acclient.c:426126): `case 47: SetAtIndex(0, 64); return DoCommand` ('/' becomes '@'); `case 64: return DoCommand`; `case 58/59` (':' and ';') builds "@emote" + rest, then DoCommand. areas.area: Held/equipped item attachment (parenting, holding locations, placement frames)
areas.summary: I compared holtburger-web's held-item path with OpenAC and the retail decomp. On the holtburger side that covers attachChildToParent, _detachChild, _replayLastAttach, _applyChildPlacementFrames, flushWieldedDirty, the ParentEvent/PickupEvent arms in objects.rs and the holtburger-world inventory handler. On the OpenAC side it covers EquippedChildAttachment, EquippedChildRenderController, ParentAttachmentState and InboundPhysicsStateController. In the decomp I read set_parent/add_child/UpdateChild/UpdateParts/SetPlacementFrame/Do+HandleParentEvent/Do+HandlePickupEvent/HandleReceivedPosition/SetChildren and the CreateObject path. Several things already match retail: mount part, root fallback for an out-of-range part, parent-first update through the three.js scene graph, the requested→Default placement fallback, and HIDDEN parents hiding their children. The biggest gaps are about authority and lifecycle, not the mount maths. (1) A held item inherits its wielder's obj_scale, because three.js scales everything parented under the wielder. Retail's Frame::combine carries no scale, so the item stays its own size and the hold offset is not scaled. This affects about 467 scaled armed creatures in the LSD sample. (2) A JS re-attach ledger (_lastAttach) re-mounts an item even when the server has just placed it on the ground. Retail only takes a parent from the PhysicsDesc. (3) ParentEvent/PickupEvent ignore their instance/position stamps, and JS throws away every position for a held item, so a newer server position can never un-parent it the way retail's HandleReceivedPosition does. (4) PickupEvent destroys the item's rig instead of leave_world, so every missile shot tears down and rebuilds the ammo rig, which also loses its ObjDesc. (5) The async attach has no generation check, so an older request can finish last and win. (6) Some fallbacks are not retail: the equip-mask location guess, mounting at the wielder's feet when the hold location is missing, and remapping ammo to the quiver.

findings.title: Held child inherits the wielder's obj_scale / ScaleHook / jump-squash scale through the three.js part node; retail draws the child at its own scale with an unscaled holding offset
findings.decomp_evidence: CPhysicsObj::UpdateChild acclient.c:320039-320057: `Frame::combine(&new_frame, &v4->parts[part_index]->pos.frame, child_frame); CPhysicsObj::set_frame(child_obj, &new_frame);`. Frame is origin+quat only, so no scale reaches the child. CPhysicsObj::add_child :316729-316760 stores the raw holding Frame (`CHILDLIST::add_child(v3->children, obj, (Frame *)&v6[1].hash_next, part, where)`). The parent's scale only multiplies the anim-frame origin of its own parts: CPartArray::UpdateParts :326601 `Frame::combine(&parts[i]->pos.frame, frame, &v3->frame[v6], &v2->scale)` → Frame::combine(scale) :326563 `v5 = _f2->m_fOrigin.x * scale->x`. The child's mesh size comes only from its own part_array scale (CPartArray::SetScaleInternal :326182: gfxobj_scale = default_scale * this->scale). CPhysicsObj::SetScale :320622 and SetScaleStatic :319008 never touch children.
findings.openac_evidence: src/AcDream.Core/Meshing/EquippedChildAttachment.cs:132 `Matrix4x4 childRoot = holdingFrame * parentPart;` (unscaled holding frame). :152-160: child visual = DefaultScale * partFrame, then `if (childScale != 1.0f) visualChildPart *= CreateScale(childScale)`, i.e. the child's own scale only. EquippedChildRenderController.cs:441 takes the scale from childSpawn.ObjScale. :638 rejects a parent world pose that carries scale (`Vector3.DistanceSquared(scale, Vector3.One) > 1e-6f`). Test tests/AcDream.Core.Tests/Meshing/EquippedChildAttachmentTests.cs:156 ChildRigidPoseExcludesDefaultScaleAndScalesOnlyOrigin.
findings.holt_evidence: scene3d/entities.js:5003-5006 `inst._baseScale = ...objScale...; root.scale.setScalar(inst._baseScale)` puts the scale on the wielder ROOT. attachChildToParent :6716-6717 `mount.add(c.root)` under `p.parts[loc.partId]`, and :6736 `c.root.position.set(loc.ox, loc.oy, loc.oz)`. The comment at :6744 claims 'The wielder root may carry obj_scale; the child inherits it through the part node ... matches retail'. The decomp contradicts this. Other root-scale writers also reach the child: the jump squash `inst.root.scale.set(base, base, base * scaleZ)` :10290 and the _tickScaleHookTween root.scale writes. LSD sample: 467 creature weenies with DefaultScale≠1 and a wield createList, e.g. Guardian Golem 1.3, Gurog Soldier 1.3, Platinum Legion Castle Guard 1.2.
findings.discrepancy: For a wielder with scale s, holtburger draws the weapon at s·s_child and places it s× farther from the hand bone. Retail draws it at s_child, offset by the raw holding frame from the (scaled) hand position. A 1.3× golem's sword is 30% too big and floats off the grip.
findings.proposed_change: In attachChildToParent, after the mount, cancel the parent's uniform scale: `const ps = p._scaleNow || p.root.scale.x || 1; c.root.position.set(loc.ox/ps, loc.oy/ps, loc.oz/ps); c.root.scale.setScalar((c._baseScale || 1)/ps); c._attachLoc = loc;`. Add `_syncAttachedChildScale(parentInst)` to recompute this for every guid in parentInst._attachedChildren. Call it at the end of _tickScaleHookTween and after each runtime objScale change. For the jump squash, compensate only the uniform `base` term; the squash itself is cosmetic. In _detachChild, restore `c.root.scale.setScalar(c._baseScale || 1)`. Fix the misleading comment at :6744.

findings.decomp_evidence: ACCObjectMaint CreateObject path acclient.c:391950-391961: `CObjectMaint::SetChildren(obj, physicsdesc); v16 = PhysicsDesc::get_parent_id(physicsdesc); if (v16) { ... CPhysicsObj::set_parent(obj, parent, PhysicsDesc::get_parent_location_id(..)); }`. The link is rebuilt only from the wire PhysicsDesc. findings.holt_evidence: remove() entities.js:12408-12417 unlinks a removed child from its wielder but deliberately keeps `_lastAttach`. _replayLastAttach :7026-7036 runs on every spawn commit (:5344): `const last = this._lastAttach.get(g); ... if (inst && inst._attachedParentGuid == null && wielder) this.attachChildToParent(g, last.parentGuid, ...)`. It does this without checking whether the new CreateObject carried a world Position and no Parent. ACE sends observers a DeleteObject (not a ParentEvent/PickupEvent) when someone unequips: ACE Player_Tracking.cs:131-152 RemoveTrackedEquippedObject → `new GameMessageDeleteObject(worldObject)`. _tickDynamicLod (:14902+) does not skip attached children. B then drops S on the ground (observer gets a fresh CreateObject with a Position and no Parent). _replayLastAttach mounts S back into B's hand, and the setPose attached-child guard then ignores every later position for S. (2) In _tickDynamicLod, add `if (inst._attachedParentGuid != null) continue;` (EQUIP-3 at :4080-4100 already says a parented object has no distance of its own). This removes the only internal respawn that builds a world-pose meta for an attached child. applyAppearance already re-mounts through selfAttach. findings.title: ParentEvent/PickupEvent ignore instance + position stamps, and JS drops every position for a held item; retail gates on the stamps and lets a newer UpdatePosition un-parent the item
findings.decomp_evidence: SmartBox::HandleParentEvent acclient.c:144512-144552: the parent's instance stamp must equal ts1 (newer → QueueBlobForObject, older → result 2/drop). The child must exist. SmartBox::DoParentEvent :143504-143528 applies only if the stamp is newer than `child->update_times[0]`, records it, then calls `set_parent(child, parent, child_location); SetPlacementFrame(child, placement_id, 1)`. HandlePickupEvent :144473-144508 and DoPickupEvent :143483-143500 use the same gate, then `unset_parent(object); leave_world(object)`. SmartBox::HandleReceivedPosition :145167-145196: after newer_event(POSITION) and the teleport check, `CPhysicsObj::unset_parent(object); if (!HasAnims(object)) SetPlacementFrame(object, placement_id, 1);` then MoveOrTeleport. A newer server position un-parents a held object.
findings.openac_evidence: src/AcDream.Runtime/Entities/InboundPhysicsStateController.cs:167-180 TryApplyPickup → `gate.TryAcceptPositionChannelEvent(update.InstanceSequence, update.PositionSequence)`. :241-252 TryApplyParent requires `parentGate.IsCurrentInstance(update.ParentInstanceSequence)` and `childGate.TryAcceptPositionChannelEvent(..., update.ChildPositionSequence)`. src/AcDream.App/Physics/LiveEntityNetworkUpdateController.cs:1031-1047: an accepted position on an attached child → `_equippedChildRenderer?.OnChildBecameUnparented(...)` → RecoverProjection in the world.
findings.holt_evidence: The stamps are parsed but unused: crates/holtburger-protocol/src/messages/object/messages/properties.rs:158-165 (parent_instance_sequence, child_position_sequence). crates/holtburger-world/src/handlers/inventory.rs:82-136 ParentEvent sets physics_parent_id/Placement/ParentLocation and pushes EntityAttached with no gate. :138-155 PickupEvent has no gate and does not clear physics_parent_id. apps/holtburger-web/src/session/messages/objects.rs:923 (ParentEvent) and :1149 (PickupEvent) emit kind=7 / KIND_REMOVE unconditionally. Entity::apply_server_position_update (crates/holtburger-world/src/entity.rs:1128-1195) compares against sequences[OBJECT_POSITION_SEQUENCE_INDEX], which ParentEvent/PickupEvent never advance. To cope, JS setPose (scene3d/entities.js:6301-6305) and applyManagedPose drop EVERY position for an attached child ('ACE keeps broadcasting a position for an equipped item in some flows (drop/pickup echo, teleport re-sync)'). ACE stamps both events with `GetNextSequence(SequenceType.ObjectPosition)` (ace-server .../GameMessageParentEvent.cs, GameMessagePickupEvent.cs), so the stamps are live.
findings.discrepancy: Stale or reordered ParentEvent/PickupEvent apply anyway. A stale UpdatePosition echo for a held item is accepted by the world model, because the ParentEvent never raised the position stamp. JS papers over this by ignoring every position for held items. As a side effect, a genuinely newer position, which retail uses to un-parent (drop-to-ground echo), can never detach the item. The UpdatePosition placement_id (PositionPack.placement_id) is also never applied (KIND_POSITION sends placement_id: 0).
findings.proposed_change: In entity.rs, add `Entity::accept_position_channel_event(instance: u16, position_seq: u16) -> bool`, modelled on accept_set_state_sequence: an older instance rejects; position_seq must be is_newer_u16 than sequences[POSITION]; record it. inventory.rs ParentEvent: require `entities.get(parent).sequences[INSTANCE] == data.parent_instance_sequence` (older → drop), then the child gate on child_position_sequence. PickupEvent: gate on its own instance+position stamp and set `physics_parent_id = None` (retail unset_parent). Expose the verdict (e.g. return false or keep a per-guid rejected set) so the objects.rs arms skip their kind=7 / REMOVE emission for rejected events. In WorldState::apply_entity_position_pack (state/mutations.rs:943): when accepted and `physics_parent_id.is_some()`, clear it and push WorldEvent::EntityDetached so position.rs emits a kind=7 parent=0 BEFORE the KIND_POSITION. Carry pos_pack.placement_id so JS can apply the resting placement (retail SetPlacementFrame). Keep the JS setPose guard only as a fallback for positions that arrive while still mounted.
findings.test_plan: Rust #[test]s in crates/holtburger-world/src/state/tests.rs, next to the existing ParentEvent (≈:3578) and PickupEvent (≈:4086) tests.
