findings.title: Async attachChildToParent / _applyChildPlacementFrames have no per-child generation check, so a stale attach or placement can land after a newer detach, re-parent or remove
findings.decomp_evidence: SmartBox::DoParentEvent acclient.c:143504-143528 runs set_parent and SetPlacementFrame synchronously in one call, in message arrival order and stamp-gated. The last accepted event always wins. DoPickupEvent :143483 likewise un-parents synchronously.
findings.openac_evidence: src/AcDream.App/Rendering/EquippedChildRenderController.cs:486 and :523 re-check `!Relations.IsPending(pending, candidateKind)` and `IsCurrentRecord(...)` after the materialization work and abandon a superseded relation. src/AcDream.Runtime/Entities/ParentAttachmentState.cs:374-389 keeps an ordered per-child relation queue.
findings.holt_evidence: scene3d/entities.js attachChildToParent (:6633) awaits `_resolveHoldingLocation` (:6651). The await yields even on a cache hit. After it, the code only checks that both rigs still exist and re-parks the request if not; it never asks whether a newer request superseded this one. _detachChild (:6828) is synchronous. _applyChildPlacementFrames (:6913) awaits `fetchFn(sid, placement)` (:6927), then checks only `if (!c || !c.parts) return;` (:6950) before writing the frames for its own `placement`. The drain calls attachChildToParent without awaiting (scene3d/loop.js:3926). Three producers feed it: kind=7, the rAF flushWieldedDirty heuristic, and the kind:47 detach handler in scene3d/index.js.
findings.discrepancy: Example 1: an attach and a later detach for the same child in one drain batch. The detach runs first, then the resumed attach re-mounts the child and re-inserts `_lastAttach`. Example 2: the child is removed meanwhile, and the resumed attach re-parks a stale request that can mount a later re-creation. Example 3: two attaches with different placements whose frame fetches resolve out of order leave the older grip pose on the parts, which is the B5 'vertical spear' symptom.
findings.proposed_change: Add `this._attachGen = new Map()`. At entry of attachChildToParent, _detachChild and remove(child), bump `gen = (this._attachGen.get(c)|0)+1`. In attachChildToParent, capture gen. After every await, `if (this._attachGen.get(cGuid) !== gen) return;`, without re-parking. Pass gen into _applyChildPlacementFrames and re-check it after its await, together with `c._attachedParentGuid === pGuid && c._attachedPlacement === placement`. Delete the entry when the child is finally removed so the map does not grow.
findings.test_plan: New tests/held_attach_generation.test.mjs (EntityManager via harness/lib/scene3d_stubs.mjs). Case 1: stub _resolveHoldingLocation with a manually resolved promise, call attachChildToParent(C,P,1,1), then _detachChild(C), then resolve. Assert C is not under P, _lastAttach has no C, and nothing is parked. Case 2: attach(C,P,1,0) with a slow placement fetch, then attach(C,P,1,1) with a fast one. Resolve the slow one last and assert the parts carry placement-1 frames.

areas.area: Fellowship, trade and allegiance state machines
areas.summary: I compared holtburger-web's trade, fellowship and allegiance code against OpenAC and the retail decomp, with vanilla ACE as the server check. The holtburger pieces I compared were the world crate handlers and state, the wasm snapshot publishers and recv-loop arms, and the trade, fellowship and allegiance panels. The OpenAC pieces were RuntimeTrade/Fellowship/AllegianceState, the fellowship event sink, the request builders and the trade-state tests. The decomp code was ClientTradeSystem/gmSecureTradeUI, ClientFellowshipSystem/gmFellowshipUI, ClientAllegianceSystem/gmAllegianceUI, and the AllegianceHierarchy unpack and patron lookup. The fellowship roster logic and the wire parse orders (Fellowship::UnPack, AllegianceHierarchy records) are correct. There are 6 real divergences, and the 2 allegiance ones are serious. (1) holtburger never sends AllegianceUpdateRequest 0x001F. Retail sends it when the player description arrives and when the allegiance panel opens. ACE never pushes the allegiance tree at login, so a sworn character's panel stays empty until someone swears or breaks. (2) When the patron is the monarch, ACE leaves out the patron record and the wasm snapshot ends up with patron=None. The panel then labels the row "Monarch" instead of "Patron / Monarch", disables Break and enables Swear. Retail's GetPatron returns the monarch in this case. (3) The trade handler treats DeclineTrade, ClearTradeAcceptance and TradeFailure the same way: it clears both accept flags. Retail clears only the side that declined. On ClearTradeAcceptance retail also empties both item lists, and ACE empties both ItemsInTradeWindow. holtburger keeps showing offers the server has already dropped, and its UI shows my acceptance cleared while ACE still counts it. (4) The trade range check never closes the trade when the partner object disappears. Retail's ObjectsInRange treats a missing object as out of range, and ACE does not close trades when a player teleports. (5) The fellowship Open/Close toggle (0x0291) is missing: ACE supports it and OpenAC has it. (6) The fellowship chat lines use made-up wording, not the retail client-side strings, which OpenAC copies exactly. None of these change rendering. Findings 1, 2 (the Rust part), 3 and 5 need a wasm rebuild; 4 is JS-only. I found no stale-state problem after disconnect: all the social snapshot cells are created fresh on each connect.

findings.title: AllegianceUpdateRequest (0x001F) is never sent, so the allegiance panel is empty after every login; Refresh sends the officer-only InfoRequest instead
findings.decomp_evidence: gmAllegianceUI::RecvNotice_PlayerDescReceived (acclient.c:204104-204113) ends with `CM_Allegiance::Event_UpdateRequest(1);`, so retail asks for the tree as soon as the player description arrives. gmAllegianceUI::OnVisibilityChanged (acclient.c:204393, body ~204420-204446) sends `CM_Allegiance::Event_UpdateRequest(1)` when the panel becomes visible and `Event_UpdateRequest(0)` when it hides. CM_Allegiance::Event_UpdateRequest (acclient.c:704098) packs opcode 31 (0x1F) plus a u32 i_on. Event_AllegianceInfoRequest is only reached from the /allegiance info chat command (acclient.c:416692). Its reply goes to ClientAllegianceSystem::Handle_Allegiance__AllegianceInfoResponseEvent (acclient.c:407159), which prints chat lines: "Note: An asterisk (*) indicates...", "Allegiance information for %hs%s:", "   Patron: %hs%s", "   Vassals:".
findings.openac_evidence: RuntimeAllegianceState.cs:59-70 NoteEnteredWorld() returns true once per session. GameRuntime.cs:750-756 AskTheServerAboutTheAllegiance(): `if (AllegianceOwner.NoteEnteredWorld()) session.SendAllegianceUpdateRequest(true);`. AllegianceRequests.cs:11 `AllegianceUpdateRequestOpcode = 0x001Fu`, and lines 29-31 build it with u32 on.
findings.holt_evidence: crates/holtburger-protocol/src/opcodes.rs:565-566 `// AllegianceUpdateRequest = 0x001F,` is commented out, and nothing in crates/ or apps/holtburger-web sends it (rg for AllegianceUpdateRequest only finds an unrelated PropertyBool). In plugins/allegiance-panel.js:675-680 the Refresh button calls `h.requestAllegianceInfo(target)` (0x027B). In ACE that action requires Seneschal (Player_Allegiance.cs:927-931 returns YouDoNotHaveAuthorityInAllegiance), and its reply goes into latest_allegiance_info (session/messages/game_event.rs ~1150-1166, kind=41), which no JS reads. The doc comment at lib.rs:52007-52016 wrongly says the reply "folds into latest_allegiance". ACE's HandleAllegianceOnLogin (Player_Allegiance.cs) sends only the MOTD and login notices, never GameEventAllegianceUpdate. ACE pushes the tree only on Rebuild (swear/break/admin) or in reply to GameActionAllegianceUpdateRequest.
findings.discrepancy: Retail asks the server for the allegiance tree when the character enters the world and whenever the panel opens, and turns the request off when the panel closes. holtburger never asks. ACE only sends the tree in reply to that request or when the allegiance changes, so playerAllegiance() is null for the whole session and the panel shows 'not in an allegiance' for sworn characters. The Refresh button sends the wrong message: ordinary members get an authority error, and for officers the reply is never shown.
findings.proposed_change: 1) Protocol: restore `AllegianceUpdateRequest = 0x001F` in opcodes.rs. Add `AllegianceUpdateRequestActionData { on: bool }` (u32 LE pack/unpack, same as FellowshipUpdateRequestActionData in messages/fellowship/actions.rs:125-146) plus a `GameAction::AllegianceUpdateRequest` variant with arms in game_action.rs. 2) wasm: add `SessionCommand::AllegianceUpdateRequest { on }` (lib.rs enum, next to FellowshipUpdateRequest at ~27310), add a send arm in session/commands/social.rs next to AllegianceInfoRequest (~762), register it in commands/mod.rs, and expose `#[wasm_bindgen(js_name = allegianceUpdateRequest)] fn allegiance_update_request(on: bool)`. 3) JS allegiance-panel.js: copy fellowship-panel.js:178-189 (ref-counted visibility) so mounting the Allegiance page or the floaty sends allegianceUpdateRequest(true) and closing the last one sends (false). Send (true) once per session after the player is in world, from an onSocialBoot hook that waits for __sessionHandle and localPlayerGuid(); this matches RecvNotice_PlayerDescReceived and OpenAC NoteEnteredWorld. Make Refresh call allegianceUpdateRequest(true). 4) Optional parity: on kind=41, print the retail InfoResponse chat lines from lastAllegianceInfoResponse, and fix the stale lib.rs doc comment.
findings.test_plan: Rust #[test] in crates/holtburger-protocol/src/messages/player/actions.rs (or wherever the new action struct goes): pack AllegianceUpdateRequest{on:true}, check the bytes are 0x1F000000 opcode + 01000000, and check unpack round-trips (the orchestrator runs it). JS: extend tests/social_panel_dom.test.mjs with a stub window.__sessionHandle that records allegianceUpdateRequest calls. Assert that mounting the allegiance page calls it with (true) exactly once, closing calls (false), opening the floaty while the tab is open sends nothing new (ref count), and Refresh calls (true) rather than requestAllegianceInfo. Run with `node tests/social_panel_dom.test.mjs`.

findings.title: When the patron is the monarch, the snapshot has patron=None, so the panel shows 'Monarch', disables Break and enables Swear
findings.decomp_evidence: AllegianceHierarchy::UnPack (acclient.c:482324, record loop ~482476-482497) reads the monarch's AllegianceData first, then each later record's parent id and data, and attaches it to the tree with `AllegianceHierarchy::Add(v4, v21 /*parent*/, &data)`. AllegianceHierarchy::GetPatron (acclient.c:481833) is `Search(id, m_pMonarch)->_patron`. For a character sworn directly to the monarch, the self node was added under the monarch, so GetPatron returns the monarch.
findings.openac_evidence: src/AcDream.Core.Net/Messages/ClientCommandResponses.cs:144-153 FindPatron: `foreach (record in records) if (record.CharacterId == guid) return FindData(monarch, records, record.ParentGuid);`. FindData (lines 133-142) checks the monarch first, so a direct vassal's patron resolves to the monarch.
findings.holt_evidence: ACE AllegianceHierarchy.cs:104-129 (ace-server Network/Structure): `if (node.Patron != null && !node.Patron.IsMonarch)` is the only path that writes a patron record, and the self record carries `node.Patron.PlayerGuid` (the monarch) as its tree parent. In holtburger apps/holtburger-web/src/lib.rs:43784-43795 publish_player_allegiance_snapshot, patron is set only from a record that is not own_guid: `else if tree_parent.0 == monarch_guid && patron.is_none() && !player_is_monarch { patron = Some(member) }`. So in the merged case patron stays None. In plugins/allegiance-panel.js, line 119 gives `patronIsMonarch` = false, line 131 `hasPatron: !!patron` = false, line 156 `brk: !!vm?.hasPatron` = Break disabled, and line 154 enables Swear. tests/social_panel.test.mjs:153-162 tests the merged case with `patron: M(1,"Boss")`, a shape the wasm never produces against ACE.
findings.discrepancy: Every first-tier vassal (patron == monarch, the most common case) sees 'Monarch' rather than 'Patron / Monarch'. They get no XP-produced frame, cannot break allegiance from the panel (breakTarget is null), and get an enabled Swear button that ACE rejects. Retail resolves the patron through the tree's parent link.
findings.proposed_change: Rust (the retail-correct fix): in publish_player_allegiance_snapshot, remember `my_parent = tree_parent` when `entry.character_id == own_guid`. After the loop, resolve the patron the way GetPatron does: use the record whose guid == my_parent, or `monarch.clone()` if my_parent == monarch_guid. Bucket everything whose parent is own_guid as vassals, so the 'first direct child of monarch is the patron' guess (which also breaks when own_guid==0) can go. Move the bucketing into a pure, non-cfg(wasm32) fn `split_allegiance_records(monarch_guid, own_guid, &[(u32 parent, Member)]) -> (Option<patron>, Option<myself>, Vec<vassals>)` so it can be host-tested. JS (works without a rebuild): in buildAllegianceViewModel (allegiance-panel.js:113-118), add `const patron = member(snap.patron) ?? ((myself && monarch) ? monarch : null);`. A non-monarch member with no patron record can only be a direct vassal of the monarch under ACE's packing.
findings.test_plan: JS: add a case to tests/social_panel.test.mjs with the ACE-shaped snapshot `{monarch: M(1,'Boss'), patron: null, myself: M(9,'Me',{cpTithed:777}), vassals: []}`. Expect vm.monarch.label === 'Patron / Monarch', vm.hasPatron === true, vm.breakTarget deepEquals {guid:1,name:'Boss'}, allegianceButtonStates(vm,{...}).brk === true and swear === false. Run with `node tests/social_panel.test.mjs`. Rust: add a #[test] for split_allegiance_records in an apps/holtburger-web/src module. Cover three cases: a direct vassal (records [(M, self), (self, v1)] gives patron=M, myself=self, vassals=[v1]); a distinct patron (records [(M,P),(P,self),(self,v)]); and the player as monarch (records [(self,v1),(self,v2)]). The orchestrator runs it.

findings.title: Trade handler treats Decline, ClearTradeAcceptance and TradeFailure the same; retail clears only the decliner's flag and flushes both offers on ClearTradeAcceptance
findings.decomp_evidence: ClientTradeSystem::Handle_Trade__Recv_DeclineTrade (acclient.c:410398): `if (source == player_id) _accepted = 0; else _p_accepted = 0;`. gmSecureTradeUI::RecvNotice_DeclineTrade (251359) resets only that side's button or indicator. gmSecureTradeUI::RecvNotice_ClearTradeAcceptance (251851) calls `gmSecureTradeUI::Reset(...)`. gmSecureTradeUI::Reset (251599) calls FlushTradeLists, which empties both item lists and queues the partner's non-owned items for destruction (251201), and sets the partner indicator to state 13. ClientTradeSystem::Handle_Trade__Recv_TradeFailure (410155): `Trade::RemoveItem(m_pTrade, i_iidItem, 1u)`, and gmSecureTradeUI::RecvNotice_TradeFailure (251924) calls RemoveAddedItem.
findings.openac_evidence: src/AcDream.Runtime/Gameplay/RuntimeTradeState.cs:167-178 ApplyDecline: `if (whoDeclined == selfGuid) _selfAccepted = false; else _partnerAccepted = false;`. tests/AcDream.Runtime.Tests/Gameplay/RuntimeTradeStateTests.cs:50-66 checks that a partner decline leaves SelfAccepted true. ApplyFailure (198-211) removes the item. Note that OpenAC ApplyClearAcceptance (213-223) also keeps the items; that is the same divergence, and the decomp wins.
findings.holt_evidence: crates/holtburger-world/src/handlers/trade.rs:27-32: `GameEvent::DeclineTrade(_) | GameEvent::ClearTradeAcceptance | GameEvent::TradeFailure(_) => { state.clear_trade_acceptance(events); }`. crates/holtburger-world/src/state/mutations.rs:2146-2152 clear_trade_acceptance sets both accepted=false and keeps both item lists. crates/holtburger-world/src/state/tests.rs:5077 test_clear_trade_acceptance_does_not_sweep_preview_entities pins the item retention. In ACE (ace-server Player_Trade.cs:188-194), ClearTradeAcceptance() runs `ItemsInTradeWindow.Clear(); TradeAccepted=false;` and is called for both players when VerifyTrade_BusyState fails or a pack is full (356-357, 424-425). HandleActionDeclineTrade (307-323) clears only the decliner's TradeAccepted. VerifyTrade_Inventory (368-376) declines just the side whose offered item has gone, while both sides were accepted. The plugins/trade-panel.js:25-26 header already claims the 'ClearTradeAcceptance → Reset' semantics that the Rust code does not implement.
findings.discrepancy: (a) After a failed finalize (too busy, too encumbered, no free slots), ACE empties both trade windows. holtburger keeps showing both offers, so re-accepting completes an empty trade while the UI showed items. (b) When one side declines, holtburger also clears the other side's acceptance. ACE still has that side accepted, so the partner pressing Trade completes the exchange even though my window shows 'not accepted'. (c) TradeFailure should drop the rejected item from my list.
findings.proposed_change: In handlers/trade.rs, split the arm. `DeclineTrade(data) => state.decline_trade(data.who_declined, events)`: a new mutation that sets self_side.accepted=false if who == player.guid, otherwise partner_side.accepted=false. `ClearTradeAcceptance => state.reset_trade(events)`: reuse the reset_trade body (mutations.rs:2133-2144), which clears both lists and both flags and sweeps partner preview entities, matching gmSecureTradeUI::Reset/FlushTradeLists. `TradeFailure(data) => state.trade_failure(data.object_guid, events)`: a new mutation that removes the guid from self_side.items (retail RemoveItem list 1), clears its trade-preview mark, and clears both flags (ACE already reset both server-side at Player_Trade.cs:121,128). Rename and invert the tests.rs:5077 test, since partner previews are swept in retail too (FlushTradeLists → AddContentsToDestructionQueue).
findings.test_plan: Rust #[test]s in crates/holtburger-world/src/state/tests.rs (the orchestrator runs them). test_decline_trade_clears_only_decliner: register a trade, set both accepted, apply decline(partner_guid), then assert self accepted is still true and partner accepted is false; do the same with decline(self). test_clear_trade_acceptance_flushes_offers replaces the :5077 test: both lists start non-empty and are empty after ClearTradeAcceptance, both flags are false, and the partner preview is swept. test_trade_failure_removes_self_item: the item is removed from self_side.items. Optionally, a handler-level test that sends GameEvent::DeclineTrade through handlers::trade::handle_event.

findings.title: Trade range watcher never closes the trade when the partner object disappears (teleport, logout, out of view), and it checks only XY distance
findings.decomp_evidence: gmSecureTradeUI::RecvNotice_RegisterTrade (acclient.c:251881) calls `CPlayerSystem::RegisterObjectRangeHandler(v8, v7, i_iidPartner, 5.0, 1 /*use radii*/, 0 /*xy_only*/, 1.0 /*interval*/, 0.0)`. CPlayerSystem::CalculateObjectRangeChecks (397612) calls `OnObjectRangeExit(objectID)` whenever ObjectsInRange is false. ACCWeenieObject::ObjectsInRange (436730) looks up both objects with GetObjectA, measures distance with `CPhysicsObj::get_distance_to_object(..., _use_radii)` (3D, since xy_only=0), and returns 0 when either object is missing. gmSecureTradeUI::OnObjectRangeExit (251819) calls CloseTradeNegotiations and Reset.
findings.openac_evidence: OpenAC has no client-side trade range close at all; it only has an explicit SendCloseTradeNegotiations (src/AcDream.Core.Net/WorldSession.cs:2418). holtburger is ahead of OpenAC here, so the decomp is the reference.
findings.holt_evidence: plugins/trade-panel.js:348-357 checkPartnerRange: line 352 `if (!me || !them) return;`, so a partner missing from entityMap (commerce_window.js:492-499 entityWorldPos returns null) never triggers the close. plugins/commerce_logic.js:290-298 isOutOfRange uses horizontalDistance (x/y only). tests/commerce_logic.test.mjs:164 pins 'unknown position never closes'. ACE closes trades only on logout (ace-server Player.cs:534-539) or on entering combat, not on teleport or portal. Both players then stay IsTrading=true, and every new trade request fails with TradeAlreadyTrading (Player_Trade.cs:56-59).
findings.discrepancy: If either player portals or recalls away, holtburger leaves the trade window open indefinitely and never sends CloseTradeNegotiations. Retail closes it on the next 1 s range check because the partner object is gone. The XY-only distance also keeps a trade open between floors that retail's 3D check would close.
findings.proposed_change: In commerce_logic.js, export a pure `tradeRangeVerdict({me, them, misses})` that returns 'close' | 'ok' | 'unknown'. It returns 'unknown' when `me` is null (scene not ready) and 'close' when `them` is null for 2 or more consecutive polls (about 1 s at the 500 ms poll, matching retail's 1.0 s interval and riding out a respawn). Otherwise it returns close/ok using a 3D distance (x, y and z, matching xy_only=0) against TRADE_RANGE + CYLINDER_RADII_ALLOWANCE. In trade-panel.js checkPartnerRange, keep a missing-partner counter, call the helper, and on 'close' run the existing chatNotice + requestClose(). Keep the old XY helper for the vendor window if it still needs it.
findings.test_plan: Extend tests/commerce_logic.test.mjs: tradeRangeVerdict({me:{x:0,y:0,z:0}, them:null, misses:1}) is 'ok' (grace) and with misses:2 is 'close'. With me:null it is 'unknown'. A partner at {x:0,y:0,z:6.5} gives 'close' (3D), and one at {x:5.9,y:0,z:0} gives 'ok'. Keep the existing isOutOfRange assertions for the vendor path. Run with `node tests/commerce_logic.test.mjs`.

findings.title: Fellowship Open/Close toggle (FellowshipChangeOpenness 0x0291) is not implemented; the leader's Open button is permanently disabled

areas.area: Object use / approach / interaction flow (world objects: double-click, toolbar Use, radial Use, UseDone)
areas.summary: I compared holtburger-web's world-object use path with retail and OpenAC. On the holtburger side that means the picking.js double-click branches, target-bar onUseClick, radial-menu Use, the SessionCommand::UseObject wire send, the UseDone and WeenieError arms in game_event.rs, and the world can_use and hydration code. On the retail side it means ItemHolder::UseObject and DetermineUseResult, CPlayerSystem::UsingItem, ClientUISystem::Handle_Item__UseDone and HandleFailureEvent. On the OpenAC side it means RuntimeWorldObjectUse, the approach driver and ItemInteractionPolicy. The overall shape in holtburger is already retail. The Use goes out at once and the server's MoveToObject does the walk (ACE CreateMoveToChain), and the busy count goes up on send and down on UseDone. OpenAC instead walks the character to the object itself (client-side MoveToObject, a 7.5 m charge rule, a 150-tick stall give-up) before sending the Use. Retail does not do that, so that driver should NOT be ported. Where holtburger is wrong is the client-side decision made before the send. The ground-pickup classifier ignores Stuck, so every Switch lever (ItemType Misc, Stuck) is sent PutItemInContainer, which ACE refuses, and the lever is never pulled. Objects retail will not use (ItemUseable=No) still get a Use, so ACE walks the player to them; in peace mode that includes monsters. The toolbar and radial Use buttons skip the pickup rule. Two smaller gaps: UseDone failures print a Rust debug label ('[Use failed] X') instead of retail's HandleFailureEvent text, and the retail 0.2 s use throttle is kept only for inventory items, not shared with the world-use paths.

areas.area: Character options, keymap and auto-* behaviour flags
areas.summary: I compared holtburger's character-option plumbing against the retail decomp, with OpenAC and ACE as cross-checks. On the holtburger side that covers holtburger-common CharacterOptions1/2 + the CharacterOption enum, the holtburger-world option mask map, the PlayerDescription option block, the wasm SetCharacterOption arm, options-panel.js, ac_character_options.js and every isCharacterOptionEnabled consumer. On the retail side it covers PlayerModule ctor/UnPack/SetOption, CPlayerModule::OnChanged/IsAutoSaveOption, ClientCombatSystem, PlaceInBackpack, AttemptPlaceIn3D and VividTargetIndicator. Several parts already match retail, so no changes are proposed for them: the bit masks and DEFAULT words (0x50C4A54A / 0x948700), the index→mask map, AutoTarget (entities.js _autoTarget), StayInChatMode (chat-panel.js:992-995 matches the ChatInterface Enter handler), ToggleRun (input.js resolveRunModifier), CoordinatesOnRadar and the fellowship-panel's own Ignore/AutoAccept exclusion. The main gap is that the Options view stores and sends many toggles that change nothing on the client. Worst of these: "Automatically accept fellowship requests" does nothing on a default character, because IgnoreFellowshipRequests defaults ON and the central path never clears it. Retail's IsAutoSaveOption batching (non-autosave options go via 0x1A1 after 480 s) is not mirrored, which makes no difference because ACE persists every SetSingleCharacterOption. ConfirmVolatileRareUse needs no client work on ACE, because ACE never sets the VolatileRare ODF bit and confirms rare gems itself (Gem.cs:76-82). The keymap's WASD/QE layout is a deliberate modernization, and I found nothing actionable in the retail keymap display.

areas.summary: I compared holtburger's plugins/radar.js, the radar helpers in scene3d/target_cycle.js and blipColorForEntity in scene3d/selection_brackets.js against retail gmRadarUI (GetBlipColor, GetBlipShape, AddObject, DrawObjects, DrawBlip, UseTime, UpdateCoordinates) and the retail functions they call (InqShowableOnRadar, GetRadarRadius, InqPlayerCoords/gid_to_lcoord, OnStatUpdated, Handle_Admin__Environs), with OpenAC's RetailRadar, RadarBlipColors and RadarSnapshotProvider as the worked reference. Most of the radar already matches retail: heading-up projection, the (range-1)^2 cut and pixel box, compass tokens, the 0.65 dim for 5 m height difference, blip pixel shapes, the selected bracket, the 6-px pick, the 75/25 m range, cell-centre coordinates in "%.1f%s,%.1f%s" with the option bit 22, and the 25 ms cadence. I found five real gaps. (1) The radar shows any object whose RadarBehavior the server never sent, using a guess, where retail hides it. (2) The blip colour/creature test treats the Attackable flag as "is a creature", so every attackable non-creature, which on ACE means almost every item, gets the gold creature colour (seen on the target brackets). (3) Other objects' PK status and blip colour come from spawn-time JS meta, so they go stale even though wasm keeps them current. (4) The radar ignores the BlackFog2 radar blackout from the admin environs message. (5) A small per-tick allocation for a debug snapshot. All fixes are JS-only and need no wasm rebuild. OpenAC has bugs of its own here (it checks UI-hidden with 0x80000000 instead of 0x80, and its radar also reads spawn-time flags), so the decompiled client is the authority throughout.

findings.title: Radar reads spawn-time meta.objDescFlags / meta.radarBlipColor, so other players' PK colour+shape go stale after a PK status change
findings.decomp_evidence: ACCWeenieObject::OnStatUpdated(int) (acclient.c:438720) handles `case 0x86u: PublicWeenieDesc::SetPlayerKillerStatus(&this->pwd, val);` (:438785), `case 0x5Fu: this->pwd._blipColor = val;` (:438779) and `case 0x85u: this->pwd._radar_enum = val;` (:438782). SetPlayerKillerStatus (acclient.c:470685) rewrites the 0x20/0x200000/0x2000000 bits. gmRadarUI::OnQualityChanged (acclient.c:263725) then calls UpdateRadarLook (GetBlipColor + GetBlipShape) for that object, or for every blip when the change is on the player.
findings.openac_evidence: src/AcDream.Core/Items/ClientObjectTable.cs:725-728 applies PlayerKillerStatusBitfield.Apply to item.PublicWeenieBitfield on an int-134 update (the live model). OpenAC's own RadarSnapshotProvider.cs:122 (`uint pwd = spawn.ObjectDescriptionFlags`) still reads spawn flags, so it has the same bug and only shows how to keep the data current.
findings.holt_evidence: plugins/radar.js:355 `const odf = (meta?.objDescFlags ?? callNum(sh, "objectDescFlags", guid) ?? 0) >>> 0;`, where meta is the scene's spawn-time meta; only a re-spawn sets meta.objDescFlags (entity_update_clone.js:114). radar.js:363-367 caches `meta.radarBlipColor` once and never refreshes it. The wasm side is already live: crates/holtburger-world/src/handlers/properties.rs:89-92 runs `refresh_pk_bits(...)` on PublicUpdatePropertyInt, which updates Entity.flags, and src/lib.rs:36728 `object_desc_flags` returns `e.flags.bits()`. ACE sends PK changes only as PublicUpdatePropertyInt(PlayerKillerStatus) (PKModifier.cs:173, Player_Death.cs:966/971/1018).
findings.discrepancy: When another player changes PK status (PK altar, or the temporary NPK after a PK death), the radar keeps the colour and shape from spawn time: red X versus white +, pink versus white. The local player's own bits come fresh from wasm (`_slow.player`), so the mutual-PK X test mixes fresh and stale data. A live RadarBlipColor update (int 95) is likewise ignored for the life of the entity.
findings.proposed_change: In radarInfoFor, use wasm first: `const wf = callNum(sh, 'objectDescFlags', guid); const odf = ((wf !== undefined && wf !== 0) ? wf : (meta?.objDescFlags ?? 0)) >>> 0;`. Read the blip colour live: `const bc = callNum(sh, 'objectIntProperty', guid, 95); blipColor = bc !== undefined ? (bc >>> 0) : (meta?.radarBlipColor ?? callNum(sh, 'entityRadarBlipColor', guid) ?? 0);`, and stop writing it permanently into meta. Optionally clear the `_info` entry for a guid when a PropertiesUpdated event for int 95/133/134 arrives, instead of waiting out the 2 s INFO_TTL. Put this in a small exported pure helper, e.g. `resolveRadarLook(sh, guid, meta)`, so it can be tested. The entities.js:8014-8024 bracket tint has the same stale meta and could use the same helper.
findings.test_plan: Export the helper from radar.js and add cases to test_radar_projection.mjs. A fake handle returning objectDescFlags 0x28 (Player|PK) with meta {objDescFlags: 0x08} gives odf 0x28, and blipShapeFor against a PK player gives X. A handle returning 0 (unknown guid) falls back to meta. objectIntProperty(95) = 8 gives the yellow blip colour even when meta.radarBlipColor = 0. Run: node test_radar_projection.mjs. The Rust side is already pinned by properties.rs pk_status_tests.
findings.already_tracked: no (Rust half fixed: properties.rs refresh_pk_bits; JS radar still reads spawn meta)

Options 0 to 5 and 9999 reach LABEL_46, which sets `m_bRadarBlank = 0`. findings.holt_evidence: app/client_events.js:2056-2070 ENVIRON_CHANGE handles only fog (`if (ec <= 0x06) { ... window.__environFogOverride = ec === 0x00 ? null : ... }`) and sounds (>= 0x65). findings.proposed_change: Export a pure `radarBlankAfterEnviron(prevBlank, option)` from radar.js: 6 gives true; 0-5 and 9999 give false; anything else returns prevBlank. In client_events.js ENVIRON_CHANGE, set `window.__radarBlank = radarBlankAfterEnviron(!!window.__radarBlank, ec)` (or call a `window.__radar.setBlank`). In radar.js update(), when blank, skip the two drawPixels calls at 870-871 but still push into `drawn` so hover and click work as in retail, and keep drawing CENTRE_PIXELS. Reset the flag on teardown/logout.

findings.title: Debug snapshot object rebuilt every 25 ms radar tick (per-blip hex strings + token style reads) with no consumer
findings.decomp_evidence: n/a (perf). Retail gmRadarUI::UseTime (acclient.c:264347) repaints every 0.025 s and keeps no extra per-tick state beyond m_aRadarInfos.
findings.openac_evidence: src/AcDream.App/UI/Layout/RadarSnapshotProvider.cs reuses `_blipScratch` and `_candidateScratch` lists; its comment says a list per refresh 'was one of the last per-frame allocations left'.
findings.holt_evidence: plugins/radar.js:884 `_lastSnapshot = { ... tokens: Object.fromEntries([...].map((d) => [d, { left: parseInt(tokens[d].style.left, 10), ... }])), blips: drawn.map((b) => ({ guid: `0x${b.guid.toString(16).padStart(8, "0")}`, ... })) }` runs on every update() (40 Hz). Its only reader is `window.__radar.snapshot()` (debug; no other references in the repo).
findings.discrepancy: About 40 snapshot objects per second, plus one string and one object per blip, are allocated only for a debug hook nobody calls in normal play. That is avoidable GC churn on a HUD loop already tuned for perf (commit 7d99b68a).
findings.proposed_change: Store the raw per-tick values (source, heading, range, cellId, coordsText, the `drawn` array reference, locked) in a small reused record and build the formatted JSON inside `snapshot()` on demand.
